text: The source-lock helper compares documented inputs with their recorded SHA256 hashes. A normal build refuses changed input bytes. Review producer changes before requesting a lock refresh. Source-lock helper # this_file: scripts/source_lock.py """Pin the exact API source bytes across checkout and installed-artifact builds.""" import json from pathlib import Path def input_hashes ( inputs : list [ dict ]) -> dict [ str , str ]: """Reject duplicate input identities instead of silently dropping their bytes.""" actual = {} for row in inputs : if row [ "source" ] in actual : raise ValueError ( "Duplicate API source input: " + row [ "source" ]) actual [ row [ "source" ]] = row [ "sha256" ] return actual def verify_inputs ( locked : dict [ str , str ], inputs : list [ dict ]) -> None : """Fail for missing, new or modified source; never silently refresh a lock.""" actual = input_hashes ( inputs ) changed = sorted ( name for name in locked . keys () | actual . keys () if locked . get ( name ) != actual . get ( name ) ) if changed : raise ValueError ( "API source lock differs: " + ", " . join ( changed [: 10 ]) + "; use --update-source-lock after reviewing source changes." ) def apply_lock ( path : Path , inputs : list [ dict ], * , update : bool ) -> dict : """Write only when explicitly requested; ordinary builds verify the pin.""" sources = input_hashes ( inputs ) if update : path . write_text ( json . dumps ( { "schema_version" : 1 , "sources" : sources , }, indent = 2 , sort_keys = True , ) + " \n " ) if not path . exists (): raise FileNotFoundError ( "API source lock missing; use --update-source-lock." ) lock = json . loads ( path . read_text ()) verify_inputs ( lock [ "sources" ], inputs ) return lock

text: A report can declare every name it captured while missing an entire namespace. Echopy now restores the useful discovery behavior of the retained introspection tools: it combines advertised and stored names, discovers loaded PythonQt children and tries qualified imports when a child is absent from the root. It preserves ordinary inspection failures instead of silently counting them as successful absence. These five independent experiments use owned Python objects and the actual maintained tooling. Run each block in a fresh namespace. They require the discovery repair from Echopy's issue-123-capture-discovery-20261102 feature; older versions omit some of these scopes. No FontLab, Qt, native framework, font, preference or user document is accessed. Temporary generated declarations in the last experiment belong only to its disposable owned directory. The experiments verify source behavior, not the deployed FontLab API. Existing native-capture, generated-reference, source-lock, site and publication holds remain in force. A successful example does not authorize refreshing those inputs. For live attribute delegation, see native values and aliases .
title: Find API scopes before measuring declaration coverage

text: dir() is useful discovery evidence, but a custom implementation can omit public dictionary names. The collector unions both sources, removes duplicates and dunder names, and sorts the result. It records names and types rather than values. from types import ModuleType from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace class Partial ( ModuleType ): def __dir__ ( self ): return [ "advertised" , "advertised" , "__doc__" ] owned = Partial ( "owned_example" ) owned . advertised , owned . stored = 1 , 2 scope = namespace ( owned , owned . __name__ ) assert scope [ "names" ] == [ "advertised" , "stored" ] assert scope [ "errors" ] == [] assert all ( "value" not in item for item in scope [ "attributes" ])
title: Retain names hidden by a custom directory listing

text: PythonQt can expose pseudo-namespaces as root attributes, separately registered modules, or importable children. Resolution prefers the root object, then the registered immediate child, then a qualified import. A registry name such as PythonQt.A.B identifies candidate A ; it does not invent a flattened A.B . Registry keys are snapshotted before imports can modify them. This experiment temporarily installs only owned module entries and restores them on leaving the context. Empty seeds keep the experiment entirely within those owned objects; they do not model every actual PythonQt namespace. import sys from types import ModuleType from unittest.mock import patch from fontlab_echopy.tooling import capture as tool root = ModuleType ( "PythonQt" ) registered = ModuleType ( "PythonQt.QtOwnedGuide" ) registered . from_registry = 1 with patch . dict ( sys . modules , { "PythonQt" : root , registered . __name__ : registered }): with patch . object ( tool , "QT_SEEDS" , ()): first = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert first [ "subpackages" ][ "QtOwnedGuide" ][ "namespace" ][ "names" ] == [ "from_registry" ] authoritative = ModuleType ( "PythonQt.QtOwnedGuide" ) authoritative . from_root = 1 root . QtOwnedGuide = authoritative second = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert second [ "subpackages" ][ "QtOwnedGuide" ][ "namespace" ][ "names" ] == [ "from_root" ]
title: Discover a loaded child without replacing the root's object

text: An import reporting that the requested child does not exist is an optional absence. A missing dependency inside that child is an inspection failure. The latter keeps its child name and exception type in the report; it must not become a successful empty namespace. Exception messages and local paths are not copied into the error record. The following import hook is an owned experiment, not a substitute implementation of discovery. from types import ModuleType from unittest.mock import patch from fontlab_echopy.tooling import capture as tool def missing_dependency ( name ): raise ModuleNotFoundError ( "owned failure" , name = "owned_dependency" ) root = ModuleType ( "PythonQt" ) with patch . object ( tool , "resolve" , return_value = root ): with patch . object ( tool , "QT_SEEDS" , ( "QtOwnedGuide" ,)): with patch ( "importlib.import_module" , side_effect = missing_dependency ): item = tool . capture ([ "PythonQt" ])[ "modules" ][ "PythonQt" ] assert item [ "subpackages" ] == {} assert item [ "namespace" ][ "errors" ] == [{ "name" : "QtOwnedGuide" , "error" : "ModuleNotFoundError" }]
title: Distinguish an absent optional child from a broken dependency

text: Ordinary discovery errors preserve other usable scopes. Timeouts, keyboard interrupts and process-exit signals propagate. In particular, swallowing a host trace deadline can disable its execution guard. A failed root getter is recorded once and is not retried by child discovery. from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace class Deadline : def __dir__ ( self ): raise TimeoutError ( "owned deadline" ) try : namespace ( Deadline (), "owned_deadline" ) except TimeoutError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned deadline" else : raise AssertionError ( "A deadline must not become partial API success" )
title: Treat a deadline as cancellation

ClassDef )) operation = next ( node for node in cls . body if isinstance ( node , ast . FunctionDef ) and node . name == "operation" ) assert ast . literal_eval ( operation . args . defaults [ 0 ]) == 3 Actual completeness still requires an approved capture from the intended FontLab build, reconciliation against the real bindings and native behavior checks. title: Verify the discovered scope reaches declarations
Echopy module values and their documentation

text: Echopy keeps a native module value connected to its owner. A read through the facade sees the current object; an accepted module write or deletion reaches the native namespace. The adjacent declaration records documentation and a type without inventing an offline value. Maintainers need to check both routes: correct names alone cannot reveal a hidden write or a lost attribute docstring. This guide explains the source contract with invented, owned modules. The names owned_echopy_values , value-with-dash and _echopy_value below are test inputs, not claims that a FontLab build exposes those names. Every assignment changes an owned ModuleType object. For real native import and read-only class identity examples, start with the Echopy package guide . An arbitrary native module assignment can change application state; these examples do not authorize copying invented assignments into FontLab.
title: Echopy module values and their documentation

text: Stage What it supplies What it does not establish Capture metadata Names, recorded types, docs and inspection failures Complete getter/setter behavior or safe arbitrary introspection Raw generation Source-safe annotated names, adjacent docs and alias metadata Concrete offline values Maintained JSON overlays Targeted doc/type enrichment with explicit source attribution New measured native semantics Merged .pyi Full declarations and adjacent attribute documentation A runtime implementation Tiny .py facade Current native dispatch, or offline declarations Emulation of FontLab Griffe static visitor What a documentation consumer reads from source Native argument conversion or execution from module import value follows normal Python binding rules: the local name refers to the object obtained at that moment. Keep reading module.value when you need later module replacements. Similarly, module.__dict__ can contain initial binding snapshots and runtime bookkeeping. Use attribute access, aliases and dir() to test delegation; do not treat the dictionary as a live native map. Python documents module subclasses in its module attribute access reference .
title: Follow a value through the pipeline

text: Use Python 3.11 in a fresh directory that you own, with the Echopy revision being checked and its docs extra already provisioned ( griffe is required). Check fontlab_echopy.__file__ before proceeding so the source or installed copy is unambiguous. No FontLab, native Qt or macOS framework is required. The source runner and installed-prefix runner execute this exact setup anew before each marked example; they never rewrite the setup or example body. Save this setup followed by one marked example in a Python file and run that file. Each example is independent. TemporaryDirectory owns the raw/merged outputs and overlays; leaving the context removes those scratch files and the invented module registrations, even if an assertion fails. The helper calls the real capture/generation/merge/runtime code rather than reproducing its logic. import ast from contextlib import contextmanager import copy import json from pathlib import Path import sys from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from types import ModuleType , SimpleNamespace from fontlab_echopy.tooling.capture import namespace as capture_namespace from fontlab_echopy.tooling.generate import generate , source_name from fontlab_echopy.tooling.merge import merge OWNED_NATIVE = "owned_echopy_values" OWNED_FACADE = "owned_echopy_values_facade" @contextmanager def owned_pipeline ( scope , * , values = None , overlays = (), stage = "merged" ): assert OWNED_NATIVE not in sys . modules and OWNED_FACADE not in sys . modules data = { "modules" : { OWNED_NATIVE : { "namespace" : copy . deepcopy ( scope )}}} with TemporaryDirectory ( prefix = "echopy-values-" , dir = Path . cwd ()) as temporary : folder = Path ( temporary ) raw , output = folder / "raw" , folder / "merged" generate ( data , raw ) paths = [] for index , patch in enumerate ( overlays ): path = folder / f "overlay- { index } .json" path . write_text ( json . dumps ( patch . pop ( OWNED_FACADE , None ) sys . modules . pop ( OWNED_NATIVE , None ) The values=None branch deliberately omits a native module. A dictionary, including an empty dictionary, explicitly supplies an owned native module. This distinction prevents an unavailable native namespace from becoming a successful dummy. The helper verifies raw and overlay byte preservation after every normally completed example; the capture example also checks its input.
title: Set up an owned experiment

text: The first example keeps an earlier local reference, replaces the value through the facade, then changes the native owner directly. Both module reads follow the owner. The earlier local reference keeps ordinary Python snapshot semantics. initial , replacement , final = object (), object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : "value" , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { "value" : initial }) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native saved_reference = facade . value assert facade . value is native . value is initial facade . value = replacement assert facade . value is native . value is replacement native . value = final assert facade . value is native . value is final assert saved_reference is initial Echopy preserves native object identity; it does not clone a value or wrap it in a documentation object. This test proves dispatch on an owned Python module. It says nothing about whether a particular native attribute has a writable setter, accepts a type, or changes a document safely. Native setter errors propagate through either spelling. Any partial native side effects require their own preservation check.
title: Read the current object and forward a write

text: A native name that cannot appear in Python source receives a source identifier. For this invented name, source_name("value-with-dash") is value_with_dash . Use getattr / setattr / delattr for the original spelling; the source identifier supports ordinary attribute syntax. Both routes must reach the same object. Deletion must remove both visible spellings, and re-creation must reconnect them. native_name = "value-with-dash" alias = source_name ( native_name ) assert alias == "value_with_dash" initial , replacement = object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : native_name , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { native_name : initial }) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is facade . value_with_dash is initial facade . value_with_dash = replacement assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is facade . value_with_dash is replacement assert { native_name , alias } . issubset ( dir ( facade )) delattr ( facade , native_name ) assert not hasattr ( native , native_name ) assert not hasattr ( facade , native_name ) and not hasattr ( facade , alias ) assert native_name not in dir ( facade ) and alias not in dir ( facade ) setattr ( facade , alias , initial ) assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is getattr ( facade , native_name ) is initial This is module dispatch. A sanitized class-member declaration does not add a renamed member to an original native class: returning that class unchanged preserves its identity. Consult the native spelling with getattr when needed. The package import aliases echopy and fontlab_echopy are a separate mechanism; the package guide checks those.
title: Keep source-safe and native spellings connected

text: The runtime keeps _echopy_native , _echopy_name and _echopy_aliases local. Its child-facade import bookkeeping also remains special, so importing a child facade cannot overwrite a native pseudo-namespace. These rules do not reserve all _echopy_ spellings. The generator separately refuses helper-name collisions before writing output; do not broaden its refusal policy to hide valid names. This matrix exercises accepted invented names at both raw and merged stages. It writes by both spellings, checks exact runtime state identities, deletes and checks dir() again. _echopy_builtins is an accepted invented value here; raw generation selects another private import alias when that name is occupied. None of these spellings is asserted to exist in the running FontLab. for stage in ( "raw" , "merged" ): for native_name in ( "_echopy_value" , "_echopy-value" , "_echopy_value-with-dash" , "_echopy_builtins" ): for route in ( native_name , source_name ( native_name )): initial , replacement = object (), object () scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : native_name , "type" : "Any" }]} with owned_pipeline ( scope , values = { native_name : initial }, stage = stage ) as case : facade , native = case . facade , case . native state = { key : facade . __dict__ [ key ] for key in ( "_echopy_native" , "_echopy_name" , "_echopy_aliases" )} setattr ( facade , route , replacement ) assert getattr ( native , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , native_name ) is replacement assert getattr ( facade , source_name ( native_name )) is replacement assert all ( facade . __dict__ [ key ] is value for key , value in state . items ()) delattr ( facade , route ) assert not hasattr ( native , native_name ) for spelling in { native_name , source_name ( native_name )}: assert not hasattr ( facade , spelling ) and spelling not in dir ( facade )
title: Reserve exact bookkeeping fields

text: An annotation is documentation, not a value assignment. The generated source and merged sidecar record an AnnAssign without a value. Offline loading keeps the annotation while attribute reads fail. A type or doc overlay must not materialize a sentinel, None or a fabricated constant. native_name = "_echopy-value" alias = source_name ( native_name ) scope = { "attributes" : [{ "name" : native_name , "type" : "int" , "doc" : "Owned value." }]} patch = { f " { OWNED_NATIVE } . { alias } " : { "returns" : "str" , "doc" : "Owned supplement." }} for stage in ( "raw" , "merged" ): with owned_pipeline ( scope , overlays = [ patch ], stage = stage ) as case : assert case . native is None assert alias in case . facade . __annotations__ assert not hasattr ( case . facade , alias ) assert not hasattr ( case . facade , native_name ) stub = ast . parse (( case . output / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .pyi" ) . read_text ()) value = next ( node for node in stub . body if isinstance ( node , ast . AnnAssign )) assert value . value is None and ast . unparse ( value . annotation ) == "str" For callable declarations, offline operations raise NativeUnavailable ; see unavailable native operations . A missing annotation-only value instead has normal absent-attribute behavior. A dir() entry or a declared type is not proof that an offline value exists.
title: Keep annotation-only values absent offline

text: Here a property object is stored directly on a plain owned module. Reading that module member returns the descriptor itself; capture can read its documentation without invoking the property getter. The deliberately failing getter makes the boundary testable. This is not a claim that every native module getattr is side-effect free, nor permission to run a fresh capture against a live host. calls = [] def forbidden_getter ( owner ): """Owned captured descriptor documentation.""" calls . append ( owner ) raise AssertionError ( "The property getter must never run" ) owned = ModuleType ( OWNED_NATIVE ) owned . value = property ( forbidden_getter ) captured = capture_namespace ( owned , OWNED_NATIVE ) before = copy . deepcopy ( captured ) assert captured [ "attributes" ][ 0 ][ "doc" ] == forbidden_getter . __doc__ with owned_pipeline ( captured ) as case : raw_text = ( case . raw / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .py" ) . read_text () stub_text = ( case . output / f " { OWNED_NATIVE } .pyi" ) . read_text () assert forbidden_getter . __doc__ in raw_text and forbidden_getter . __doc__ in stub_text assert case . result == { "applied" : 0 , "unmatched" : []} assert captured == before and calls == [] Capture records errors explicitly. Documentation and a recorded descriptor type do not establish whether a native property is readable, writable or callable. A docstring that includes parentheses is not enough to turn an attribute into a method. Preserve recorded fields and limitations rather than guessing a setter.
title: Capture descriptor documentation without invoking its getter

text: The generator accepts module attributes , constants and modules collections. Those are input collections; capture need not classify every object into all three. text: A glyph-info manager holds several graphs at once: raw records and indexes, sidebar groups, lazy rank caches, a work queue and observer state. A new list does not necessarily mean a new index, and changing a list does not necessarily invalidate its cached order. These experiments show the actual source-derived behavior and its failure boundaries. The described implementation is pinned to Glyport 5e04d1168b4e33823bed4940fce308637f8abadd . It has source and package-archive verification. Matching Echopy declarations, ordinary installations and native FontLab workflows require their own verification. Start with metadata managers and execution profiles for lookup and complete local initialization, then sidebar trees and document metadata for projected groups, counts and URL loading. This page covers raw accessor identity, retained rank caches, debug/shared construction, observation, placeholder fonts and recovery.

text: Use glyph.glyphInfo for metadata resolved through that glyph's parent font and document. Use Glyphs.glyphInfoForName(..., font=font) or the Unicode method when you explicitly choose a font. text: The resolver selects Unicode/name metadata, applies additional Unicode, ROS and Arabic presentation stages, then applies enabled stored fields. The six fields are case , group , script , category , subCategory and direction ; their flags are storeCase , storeGroup , storeScript , storeCategory , storeSubCategory and storeDirection . Setting a raw value alone does not enable its overlay. Keep-name categories and earlier explicit refusals have their own branches; do not infer a universal overlay result from this owned letter case. manager , record = owned_manager () exports , font = owned_exports ( manager ) glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] values = { "case" : 5 , "group" : "Stored" , "script" : "greek" , "category" : "Symbol" , "subCategory" : "Math" , "direction" : 2 } baseline = { name : getattr ( glyph . glyphInfo , name ) for name in values } for name , value in values . items (): setattr ( glyph , name , value ) assert getattr ( glyph . glyphInfo , name ) == baseline [ name ] setattr ( glyph , "store" + name [ 0 ] . upper () + name [ 1 :], True ) assert getattr ( glyph . glyphInfo , name ) == value assert all ( getattr ( glyph . glyphInfo , name ) == value for name , value in values . items ()) assert ( record . case , record . group , record . script , record . category , record . subCategory , record . direction ) == ( 1 , "Local" , "latin" , "Letter" , "Owned subcategory" , 0 ) groupIdx is a separate raw signed 16-bit field, not a seventh overlay flag. Group flag transitions do not look up/reset raw group or groupIdx. Turning an enabled direction flag off resolves and stores the selected direction, and a detached direction reset refuses. In particular public group/groupIdx and physical metadata recipes remain explicit unavailable capabilities where the input does not establish them. Outline components and Unicode NFD do not supply those recipes. text: The execution profile chooses application wrapper semantics. FontLab's version or build does not identify a Glyphs generation. Direct GSApplication(...) and factory calls with no profile use Glyphs4; factory profiles must be explicit glyphs2 , glyphs3 or glyphs4 . The execution layer resolves auto before it constructs these providers. Do not combine the public Glyphs3 keyword/formatting contract with Glyphs4 integer font forwarding. text: loadCustomGlyphDataFromURL_error_(url, None) accepts the qualified path() URL protocol and returns a bool. The synthetic objc.NULL singleton is also accepted; this does not import native objc or establish arbitrary NSError output-slot/tuple bridging. Non-null error arguments refuse before reading a URL. Missing files succeed; too-short or malformed files return false. Non-regular files and unsupported UTF8/URL conversion remain explicit unavailable capabilities. The parser implements the retained glyph-token/custom-attribute contract rather than general XML normalization. Supplied file order and duplicates remain visible. Completed rows survive a later failure, and later files are not consumed. Custom description, group and legacy Unicode are not merge fields; fresh known nil/zero defaults differ from unknown maintained public data. A project-file input is not silently changed to its directory. Root repeats remain repeats. text: Continue with sidebar trees and document metadata for defaults-backed visibility, dynamic category/filter trees, insertion and copy identity, delayed counts, list expansion and actual document URL loading. Its experiments reuse the exact setups below and keep FontLab adapters explicit. The source checkpoint connects initWithLocalFile_ , initWithLocalFile_forFont_ , loadGlyphInfo and their base-parser/sidebar helpers. Public global queries can use the maintained public record index without these dependencies. Complete local initialization needs an explicit lawful provider; there is no default provider for private GlyphData, sidebar property lists, iMatra resources, localization, images, predicates or operation queues. The internal using_info_provider context supplies dependencies for source qualification. It is not a supported native provider installer. An allocated local receiver retains the exact URL object, creates its own queue, sets that queue's concurrency limit, dispatches the sidebar before glyph loading, then waits after successful loading. None is a global-load branch on that local receiver; it does not turn the receiver into the shared manager. An existing shared receiver retains its shared flag if explicitly reinitialized. The font argument selects sidebar dispatch, including the empty icon-set branch; the initializer does not establish document observation or a lasting font binding.

text: loadGlyphInfo() resets the row/category arrays, keeps the name/Unicode maps and queues a summary that reads the current rows when it executes. A custom override can update an existing indexed record without relisting it. Only listed rows receive fresh unsigned 32-bit indices and component finalization. Earlier views can remain canonical and addressable even when absent from the new row list. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( url ) index = manager . _index names , codes , old_rows = index . names , index . unicodes , index . records retained = manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "owned.local" ) data . write_text ( '<glyph name="owned.local" script="changed"/>' , encoding = "utf-8" ) manager . loadGlyphInfo () assert index . names is names and index . unicodes is codes assert index . records is not old_rows and index . records == [] assert manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "owned.local" ) is retained assert retained . script == "changed" and retained . unicode == "0042" assert manager . _lifecycle . queue . pending data . write_text ( '<glyph name="owned.new" script="fresh"/>' , encoding = "utf-8" ) manager . loadGlyphInfo () assert [ row . name for row in index . records ] == [ "owned.new" ] assert index . records [ 0 ] . index == 0 manager . _lifecycle . queue . waitUntilAllOperationsAreFinished () assert "fresh" in manager . _lifecycle . scriptIDs assert "changed" not in manager . _lifecycle . scriptIDs The local reload has no final barrier. Both queued summaries above see the latest row list. Script IDs persist across reloads and shared IDs can be appended again; do not interpret these arrays as a fresh deduplicated inventory of every map key. Nil/global loading has a Chinese intermediate barrier before later Hangul work; the constructor adds its final wait. Neither universal synchronous reload nor universal absence of waits describes both branches.
title: Reload retains maps while replacing the listed rows

text: The base scanner parses into independent containers before committing. It commits names, encodings, rows and groups in order, with separate locks rather than an atomic transaction. Empty destination containers can adopt parsed containers; nonempty containers merge. Base rows establish description/group fields that custom overrides do not merge. A malformed private parse leaves those manager containers untouched; custom parsing can retain completed earlier rows on failure. Neither scanner is a general XML normalizer or a proprietary GlyphData replacement. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( url ) base = data . parent / "base-owned.xml" base . write_text ( '<glyph name="owned.fields" unicode="0043" ' 'description="Base description" group="Base group" ' 'groupIdx="-3" script="owned"/>' , encoding = "utf-8" ) base_url = SimpleNamespace ( path = lambda : str ( base )) sentinel = object () slot = InfoErrorSlot ( sentinel ) assert manager . loadGlyphDataFromURL_error_ ( base_url , slot ) assert slot . value is sentinel view = manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "owned.fields" ) assert ( view . desc , view . group , view . groupIdx ) == ( "Base description" , "Base group" , - 3 ) override = data . parent / "override.xml" override . write_text ( '<glyph name="owned.fields" description="Ignored" ' 'group="Ignored" script="changed"/>' , encoding = "utf-8" ) assert manager . loadCustomGlyphDataFromURL_error_ ( SimpleNamespace ( path = lambda : str ( override )), None ) assert manager . infoFromDataForName_ ( "owned.fields" ) is view assert ( view . desc , view . group , view . groupIdx , view . script ) == ( "Base description" , "Base group" , - 3 , "changed" )

text: None and the synthetic objc.NULL remain the supported public null arguments. InfoErrorSlot is an internal explicit source analogue of an output slot, not an arbitrary native pointer bridge. title: Preserve caller error state and partial custom commits

text: The protected interval covers component finalization and Hangul enqueue. InfoNativeException is the owned source analogue for that qualified native exception boundary. Ordinary Python errors, dependency refusals, earlier loader failures and deferred callback failures propagate. A constructor does not drain pending work on an exceptional return. These subclasses inject failures at the actual public dispatch boundary; they do not claim a complete alternate loader. class MarkedFailure ( GSGlyphsInfo ): def updateComponentsInfos ( self ): raise InfoNativeException ( "owned component failure" ) with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = MarkedFailure . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( url ) failures = [ event [ 1 ] for event in provider . events if event [ 0 ] == "log" ] assert any ( isinstance ( error , InfoNativeException ) for error in failures ) assert manager . _lifecycle . iMatraCombinations is provider . dictionary assert not manager . _lifecycle . queue . pending assert manager . _index . records [ 0 ] . index == 0 class OrdinaryFailure ( GSGlyphsInfo ): def updateComponentsInfos ( self ): raise RuntimeError ( "owned ordinary failure" ) with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): receiver = OrdinaryFailure . alloc () try : receiver . initWithLocalFile_ ( url ) except RuntimeError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned ordinary failure" else : raise AssertionError ( "Ordinary exceptions must propagate" ) queue = receiver . _lifecycle . queue assert queue . pending and ( "wait" , queue ) not in provider . events assert receiver . _lifecycle . iMatraCombinations is None assert not any ( event [ 0 ] == "log" and isinstance ( event [ 1 ], RuntimeError ) for event in provider . events )

text: The summary takes distinct script/subcategory values from current listed rows, sorts new values with the supplied comparison policy, preserves existing repeats, adds Conjunct after Halfform when present, and removes empty strings. Each field reads the current rows separately. text: Sidebar category/language arrays are cached process-wide on first access, including a decoded nil result. Changing providers later does not refresh that cache. Custom group files retain provider order; a bad property list stops its folder after earlier mutations and schedules error presentation. An empty primary filter array suppresses fallback; an unavailable primary can select the standard resource. Extra filter headers retain filename titles, source paths and ordering. Image type checks, decoding, registration and template marking remain explicit dependencies. The fixture's empty image directories prove none of those native effects, and its recorded emoji object proves only the provider call boundary. Complete lawful default/private resources, predicates, images/counts, observation lifetime, concurrency and document reload binding remain unqualified. The following generation examples qualify actual algorithms over invented inputs; they do not qualify the missing proprietary banks or native resource loading. Python group-lock identity differs from the native current dictionary monitor; this sequential example does not establish concurrency parity. Original font workflows, native history/lifetime/preservation/save/reopen, ordinary installed tuples and complete consumers require independent evidence. Generated reference, source-lock refresh, site/archive/routes, browser accessibility and publication remain gated. The full issue remains active.

text: The queued operation visits every syllable from AC00 through D7A3 . For each one it looks up the target, leading Jamo, vowel Jamo and optional trailing Jamo, in that order. This example checks the three supplied syllable targets against Unicode NFD and checks their exact component-record identities. It exercises the complete operation even though the fixture stores only three syllable targets. Unicode NFD supplies an independent scalar oracle, not a proprietary recipe bank. import unicodedata with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , url , data ): manager = GSGlyphsInfo . alloc () . initWithLocalFile_ ( None ) for code in ( 0xAC00 , 0xAC01 , 0xD7A3 ): target = manager . _index . unicodes [ f " { code : 04X } " ] expected = tuple ( manager . _index . unicodes [ f " { ord ( part ) : 04X } " ] for part in unicodedata . normalize ( "NFD" , chr ( code ))) assert len ( expected ) == ( 2 if code == 0xAC00 else 3 ) assert target . _component_records == expected assert all ( actual is wanted for actual , wanted in zip ( target . _component_records , expected )) assert target . _locked and target . baseString == chr ( code ) view = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( f " { code : 04X } " ) assert all ( part . _resolved_record is raw for part , raw in zip ( view . components , expected )) assert not manager . _lifecycle . queue . pending

title: Legacy Unicode snapshots and ROS metadata

text: The global name factory reads maintained GlyphData. Its unicode and unicodeLegacy fields answer different questions: Requested name Canonical name unicode unicodeLegacy A A "0041" None alef-ar alef-ar "0627" None alef-ar.isol alef-ar.isol None "FE8D" aleffinalarabic alef-ar.fina None "FE8E" The owned application fixture supplies no host bridge or persistent defaults. It does not activate the synthetic GlyphsApp module. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for name , primary , legacy in [ ( "A" , "0041" , None ), ( "alef-ar" , "0627" , None ), ( "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ), ]: info = app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) Aliases resolve to the maintained canonical record, including its legacy field. They do not create a second independent primary-Unicode record. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) alias = app . glyphInfoForName ( "aleffinalarabic" ) canonical = app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.fina" ) assert alias . name == canonical . name == "alef-ar.fina" assert alias . unicode is canonical . unicode is None assert alias . unicodeLegacy == canonical . unicodeLegacy == "FE8E" The shared Unicode index includes each record’s primary keys followed by its non-nil legacy key in source order; later assignments replace earlier ones. Global Unicode lookup therefore selects alef-ar.isol for FE8D , with primary Unicode None and legacy Unicode FE8D . It selects hamza-ar.isol for FE80 and the later NULL record for duplicated 0000 . These examples qualify specific maintained records, not complete custom GlyphData. The linked guide separates exact combined-index lookup, raw synthesis on a true miss and remaining input boundaries.
title: Keep primary and legacy Unicode separate

text: Omitting font , passing positional None or using font=None selects shared data without reading the active font. An explicit font now selects that font's manager; the earlier unconditional .localData refusal is superseded. Integer Name dispatch discards font only in Glyphs2/3; Glyphs4 forwards it through the instance Unicode method. See the current manager/profile examples . The fixture below preserves active-font isolation while explicitly checking selected-manager delegation and propagation of an invalid font's access error. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class UnreadableFont : def __getattribute__ ( self , name ): raise AssertionError ( "Global lookup must not read an active font" ) active = UnreadableFont () app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = active ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , None ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = None ) . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" local = owned_parsed_manager () explicit = SimpleNamespace ( glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = explicit ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "alef-ar.isol" ) try : app . glyphInfoForName ( "alef-ar.isol" , font = active ) except AssertionError as error : assert str ( error ) == "Global lookup must not read an active font" else : raise AssertionError ( "An explicitly selected invalid font must expose its access failure" )
title: Global lookup ignores active-font data

text: Direct GSGlyphInfo construction from a namespace snapshots the supplied legacy value exactly. Missing means None ; empty strings, lowercase hex and arbitrary owned text remain distinct. Editing the source object later does not edit the snapshot. This package makes snapshots read-only and refuses assignment with GSGlyphInfo.unicodeLegacy . Native Glyph Info has a setter; package read-only policy does not describe the native object's mutability. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSGlyphInfo for legacy in ( None , "" , "fe8d" , "unparsed owned value" ): source = SimpleNamespace ( name = "owned" , unicode = None , unicodeLegacy = legacy , category = "Letter" , subCategory = None , script = "arabic" , case = 0 ) snapshot = GSGlyphInfo ( source ) source . unicodeLegacy = "changed" assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == legacy try : snapshot . unicodeLegacy = "FE8D" except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.unicodeLegacy" else : raise AssertionError ( "The package snapshot must be read-only" ) assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == legacy del source . unicodeLegacy assert GSGlyphInfo ( source ) . unicodeLegacy is None
title: Snapshot raw values without normalizing them

text: For an actual package GSGlyph , the constructor resolves only the new legacy field through owned metadata. Existing name, primary Unicode, category, subcategory, script and case snapshot behaviour is retained. This constructor does not replace those fields with a wholesale resolved record. Resolution can refuse unsupported data; it does not query a native application. An unencoded alef-ar.isol draft has a legacy value without acquiring an encoding. A generic derived suffix clears inherited legacy metadata. A nil resolved record gives no legacy value, even when the stored name resembles an isolated-form record. An already captured snapshot remains independent. Global indexing and model postprocessing are different paths. The detached, already encoded Arabic glyph below still reaches the retained parentless Arabic nil-return branch: its snapshot keeps stored primary FE8D and legacy None . Direct global lookup of FE8D returns alef-ar.isol with database primary None and legacy FE8D . The shared-index correction does not bypass the model branch. from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSGlyphInfo from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph glyph = GSGlyph ( "alef-ar.isol" ) snapshot = GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) assert ( snapshot . name , snapshot . unicode , snapshot . unicodeLegacy ) == ( "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ) assert glyph . unicodes == [] with owned_parsed_manager () . _scope (): glyph . name = "alef-ar.isol.owned" assert GSGlyphInfo ( glyph ) . unicodeLegacy is None assert snapshot . unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" encoded = GSGlyph ( "alef-ar.isol" ) encoded . unicode = "FE8D" current = GSGlyphInfo ( encoded ) assert current . unicode == "FE8D" and current . unicodeLegacy is None assert encoded . unicodes == [ "FE8D" ] assert GSGlyphInfo ( GSGlyph ( "unknown-owned" )) . unicodeLegacy is None
title: Construct from an owned model glyph

text: The audited shared manager places ROS replacement after additional Unicode and before Arabic presentation. With its actual maps, it replaces the complete ordered Unicode set using the resolved metadata name . Glyport does not bundle those proprietary MapFiles. Adobe CMaps and maintained GlyphData are not equivalent substitutes; no approximated map is supplied. The exact shared-manager text contract is: Split on a hyphen ( - ). Only when that result has a count other than three, retry with comma plus one space ( , ). Require exactly three pieces. Preserve case and whitespace. Use the first two pieces for the map name. Ignore the supplement; it need not be numeric or nonempty. Requests naming Adobe-CNS1 , Adobe-GB1 , Adobe-Japan1 , Adobe-KR or Adobe-Korea1 raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData before presentation and metadata writes. The guard cannot know whether a particular glyph would be absent from the unavailable map, so that does not bypass refusal. The revision comparison below is an explicitly owned backend diagnostic, not native dirty-state proof. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend for ordering in ( "CNS1" , "GB1" , "Japan1" , "KR" , "Korea1" ): for separator in ( "-" , ", " ): for supplement in ( "7" , "" , "owned" ): backend = FakeBackend () font = Model ( backend ) . font glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] font . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = separator . join (( "Adobe" , ordering , supplement )) before = ( glyph . name , glyph . unicodes , glyph . case , glyph . script , glyph . category ) revision = backend . revision ( "font" ) try : glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unavailable ROS mapping must refuse" ) assert ( glyph . name , glyph . unicodes , glyph . case , glyph . script , glyph . category ) == before assert backend . revision ( "font" ) == revision
title: Recognize ROS requests before writing

text: Nil, malformed text and unknown map names leave the preceding record unchanged at the ROS stage. That shared-bundle no-op does not make an entire metadata refresh a no-op: earlier additional-Unicode processing can still add encodings. It is not a guarantee about arbitrary custom managers or user-supplied resources. For example, Adobe,Japan1,7 lacks the required spaces. Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra-more has exactly three hyphen pieces, so comma fallback is suppressed and no shipped map matches. Conversely, Adobe-Japan1-7\n and Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra still require the missing map: the supplement is ignored after delimiter selection. from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend for value in ( None , "" , "Adobe-Japan1" , "Adobe-Japan1-7-extra" , "Adobe,Japan1,7" , "Adobe, Japan1, 7" , " Adobe-Japan1-7" , "adobe-Japan1-7" , "Adobe-Unknown-7" , "Adobe, Japan1, 7-extra-more" ): font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] font . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = value glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . name == "A" assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0041" , "0061" ] # Earlier additional-Unicode stage. Normal first-active parameter selection applies to ROS. An inactive or shadowed map request is not the selected value. Nontext values require an unqualified Objective-C description conversion; they raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.value rather than using Python str , truthiness or an invented native representation. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] first = GSCustomParameter ( "ROS" , "Adobe-Unknown-7" ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , GSCustomParameter ( "ROS" , "Adobe-Japan1-7" )]) glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0041" , "0061" ] first . active = False try : glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData" else : raise AssertionError ( "The now-selected map request must refuse" ) other = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font other . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () other . customParameters [ "ROS" ] = False try : other . glyphs [ "A" ] . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.value" else : raise AssertionError ( "Nontext ROS description is unqualified" )
title: Distinguish an unknown resource from a no-op refresh

title: Ordered parameters and Arabic presentation forms

text: The same collection supports two different questions: Operation Meaning parameters["Name"] Value of the first active matching parameter, or None "Name" in parameters A matching object exists, including an inactive one parameters[index] The actual ordered parameter object parameters["Name"] = value Change the first matching object, retaining its active flag; append if absent parameters["Name"] = None Remove the first matching object del parameters["Name"] Remove the first match; missing or empty names are a no-op parameters.remove(parameter) Remove that parameter object (by identity); ValueError if it is not in the collection Indexed replacement/deletion Replace/remove that position and detach the old object Do not treat name lookup as an ordinary dictionary when duplicates or inactive entries matter. A name assignment can change an inactive object while a later active duplicate still supplies the effective value. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font first = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "first" ) second = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "second" ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , second ]) assert font . customParameters [ 0 ] is first assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "first" first . active = False assert "Owned Setting" in font . customParameters assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second" font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] = "changed inactive object" assert first . value == "changed inactive object" and not first . active assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second" font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] = None assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ second ] assert first . parent is None first . value = "detached edit" assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "second"
title: Choose a value or an object

text: Insertion order is retained. insert uses strict bounds rather than clamping a large positive or negative index. A negative index adds the current length once; insert(-1, parameter) therefore inserts before the last item. Replacing or removing an object detaches it, while the supplied replacement becomes live. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font first = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned duplicate" , 1 ) later = GSCustomParameter ( "Owned duplicate" , 2 ) font . customParameters . extend ([ first , later ]) font . customParameters . remove ( later ) assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ first ] # Removal is by object identity. assert later . parent is None before = GSCustomParameter ( "Before last" , 3 ) font . customParameters . insert ( - 1 , before ) assert list ( font . customParameters ) == [ before , first ] replacement = GSCustomParameter ( "Replacement" , 4 ) font . customParameters [ - 1 ] = replacement assert first . parent is None and replacement . parent is font try : font . customParameters . insert ( 99 , GSCustomParameter ( "Outside" , 0 )) except IndexError : pass else : raise AssertionError ( "Out-of-range insertion must not clamp silently" ) Iteration captures the initial count and fetches each object as it advances. Appending does not extend an existing iterator; shrinking the collection can make its next indexed access raise IndexError . Finish iteration before editing its structure, or collect the intended positions first. Nested mutation of an attached value container is not a qualified notification route; assign the whole replacement value instead. Same-object multiple insertion, cross-owner reparenting and complete native identity remain open. A copied parameter owns its nested value but retains its recorded parent pointer; a copy is not proven to be a detached native object.
title: Keep positional edits explicit

text: A font and its masters have distinct parameter collections. Ordinary master userData excludes reserved parameter storage and preserves it when other user data changes. The presentation setting is read from the glyph's parent font ; a master parameter does not enable the font setting. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font master = font . masters [ 0 ] master . userData [ "Owned note" ] = { "tags" : [ "proof" ]} font . userData [ "Owned font data" ] = 7 master . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "master" )) font . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "Owned Setting" , "font" )) assert master . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "master" assert font . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "font" assert dict ( master . userData ) == { "Owned note" : { "tags" : [ "proof" ]}} master . userData [ "Another note" ] = 8 assert master . customParameters [ "Owned Setting" ] == "master" assert dict ( font . userData ) == { "Owned font data" : 7 } The persistence representation uses ordered records and compatible flat-key mirrors. Old flat values import in their former sorted order because the old format recorded no original insertion order or active flags. New external flat names are retained. An external edit or deletion of an existing mirrored value wins: the collection follows the flat keys, reads never raise, and one CUSTOM_PARAMETERS_REBUILT warning is queued. This storage diagnostic reconstructs a Python model over the same owned backend. It is not a native font save/reopen test: from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend from fontlab_glyport.model.proxies import CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX backend = FakeBackend () # "font" is this test backend's owned font identity, not a native font ID. backend . set_lib ( "font" , { CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX + "Z owned" : [ 1 ], CUSTOM_PARAMETER_PREFIX + "A owned" : 2 , "unrelated" : { "keep" : [ 3 ]}, }) font = Model ( backend ) . font assert [ p . name for p in font . customParameters ] == [ "A owned" , "Z owned" ] font . customParameters . append ( GSCustomParameter ( "A owned" , 4 )) font . customParameters [ 0 ] . active = False reconstructed = Model ( backend ) . font assert [( p . name , p . active ) for p in reconstructed . customParameters ] == [ ( "A owned" , False ), ( "Z owned" , True ), ( "A owned" , True ) ] assert reconstructed . customParameters [ "A owned" ] == 4 assert backend . lib ( "font" )[ "unrelated" ] == { "keep" : [ 3 ]}
title: Separate font, master and user data

text: The exact key is Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes , including its spaces and case. UseArabicPresentationFormUnicodes is a different key. Prefer an explicit Boolean for a setting; raw Python truthiness does not describe the upstream string-conversion rules. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "alef-ar" )) font . masters [ 0 ] . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] # A master setting does not enable it. font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . name == "alef-ar" assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] # Ordered deduplication. font . customParameters [ KEY ] = False glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] # Refresh removes the previous addition. The ordinary additional-Unicode helper and this presentation stage are separate. The former has its own gates and uses ordinary .isol.unicode ; legacy-only .isol data does not become a primary encoding just because that helper ran. Presentation instead reads unicodeLegacy . A separately named .isol glyph can block the earlier helper's manager lookup without blocking the presentation stage's raw legacy lookup.
title: Enable Arabic presentation encodings

text: The stage tests the resolved record's script, then uses its canonical name. A direct non-nil unicodeLegacy takes precedence. Only nil triggers a raw <resolved name>.isol database lookup. An empty string is non-nil: it blocks fallback, then adds no encoding. Additions retain order, deduplicate and follow the upstream nonempty/shorter-than-eight length gate. Generic constructed suffixes clear inherited legacy; direct database suffix records retain their own. Implemented ordering is resolution/private-use handling, the ordinary additional-Unicode helper, ROS processing, presentation processing, then stored metadata overlays. Requests for the five proprietary shipped ROS maps now refuse before presentation and metadata writes because their mapping data is unavailable. Malformed/unknown text leaves this stage unchanged under the audited shared-bundle contract. See the legacy and ROS guide for exact delimiters, supplement handling, nontext refusal and owned no-write examples. Full ROS mapping, complete local initialization/private resources and unqualified suffix routes remain outside this bounded example matrix. A stored Latin script does not suppress presentation on an Arabic resolved record; the overlay runs later. Conversely, storing Arabic script on a Latin resolved record does not make it an Arabic presentation candidate. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () alias = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "OwnedArabicAlias" )) alias . unicode = "0627" alias . storeScript = True alias . script = "latin" font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True alias . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert alias . name == "OwnedArabicAlias" and alias . script == "latin" assert alias . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ] Resetting a storage flag refreshes that metadata field without writing encodings. The next explicit refresh can apply presentation encodings. Native name-collision adjustment is a separate open route: it can clear encodings even with changeName=False . The no-conflict examples do not prove that route. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "alef-ar" )) glyph . storeScript = True glyph . script = "latin" font . customParameters [ KEY ] = True glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "arabic" and glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0627" , "FE8D" ]
title: Direct, nil and empty legacy data

text: For this exact BOOL-schema key, plain Python bool , int and float retain their numeric type and precision; None on the object becomes False . Assigning None by parameter name still removes the first matching object. A string containing the current locale's decimal separator uses real NSNumberFormatter parsing, then float32. Other strings use NSString.integerValue. The default formatter is process-cached; an explicit locale below owns a temporary formatter and changes no global preferences. Input and route Result Enables presentation? Numeric 0.5 Retained 0.5 Yes Numeric 1e-46 Retained double precision Yes String "YES" or "true" Integer 0 No String "1e-3" without the decimal separator Leading integer 1 Yes String "1.0e-46" , dot-decimal locale Float32 0.0 No String "0,5" , comma-decimal locale Float32 0.5 Yes Malformed decimal "0.5junk" , dot-decimal locale Nonzero float 2**63 sentinel Yes The failed-parse sentinel is an upstream quirk established by retained machine code and independent Foundation observations. It is not a recommendation to use malformed input. Guessing bool(text) or treating every parse failure as zero would change the setting's behaviour. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSCustomParameter , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend from fontlab_glyport.model.parameter_numbers import normalize assert normalize ( "YES" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0 assert normalize ( "true" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0 assert normalize ( "0,5" , locale_name = "de_DE" ) == 0.5 assert normalize ( "1.0e-46" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == 0.0 assert normalize ( 1e-46 ) == 1e-46 assert normalize ( "0.5junk" , locale_name = "en_US" ) == float ( 2 ** 63 ) KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes" font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font parameter = GSCustomParameter ( KEY , True ) font . customParameters . append ( parameter ) parameter . value = None assert parameter . value is False and len ( font . customParameters ) == 1 font . customParameters [ KEY ] = None assert len ( font . customParameters ) == 0 This string route is measured on macOS 27.2 arm64 Foundation, not every Foundation version. Non-macOS strings and arbitrary object/container conversions explicitly raise UnsupportedCapability ; their implementation/qualification remains open. Existing numeric NaN retains numeric enabling semantics and must not be mistaken for an external mirror conflict. Active-value cache construction validates all active duplicates, including shadowed ones. Indexed/name/active inspection and name-based removal remain available for an inactive imported value whose conversion is unsupported. Name membership is a separate object lookup that can still validate the first matching object; it is not a substitute for those recovery operations.
title: Read typed values on macOS

title: Stored production names in Glyph Info

text: Run this setup once before the examples. It temporarily substitutes a small owned in-memory dataset and restores the maintained dataset in finally . It never edits the dependency's source files or dictionaries. This is a test fixture; a normal script obtains Glyphs and the classes from its own GlyphsApp execution context. from contextlib import contextmanager from pathlib import Path from types import ModuleType from glyphsLib import glyphdata from fontlab_glyport import ExecutionContext from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp.fontlab_session import FontLabSession @contextmanager def owned_glyphs ( rows ): glyphdata . get_glyph ( "A" ) previous = glyphdata . GLYPHDATA records = [ dict ( row ) for row in rows ] names = { row [ "name" ]: row for row in records } alternatives , productions , encodings = {}, {}, {} for row in records : for alias in row . get ( "altNames" , "" ) . replace ( " " , "" ) . split ( "," ): if alias : alternatives [ alias ] = row if row . get ( "production" ): productions [ row [ "production" ]] = row if row . get ( "unicode" ): encodings [ row [ "unicode" ]] = row owned = glyphdata . GlyphData ( names , alternatives , productions , encodings ) ctx = ExecutionContext ( Path . cwd (), "glyphs3" ) session = FontLabSession ( ctx , version = ( 3.2 , 3234.0 ), packages = [], defaults = {}, qt = object (), fontlab = ModuleType ( "fontlab" ), ) ctx . adapters . update ( session . adapters ()) glyphdata . GLYPHDATA = owned try : with ctx : yield ctx . import_module ( "GlyphsApp" ) finally : ctx . close () glyphdata . GLYPHDATA = previous assert records == rows , "Queries must preserve the owned source records"

text: A known absent field is None . Empty text is a present value. Both an explicit nice-name value and a different explicit production value survive direct and exact-name reads. The raw nil example uses a fresh dataset: an earlier name query can already have filled that shared record. rows = [ { "name" : "nil" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "empty" , "unicode" : "0042" , "production" : "" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "equal" , "unicode" : "0043" , "production" : "equal" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "explicit" , "unicode" : "0044" , "production" : "OwnedProd" , "category" : "Letter" }, ] with owned_glyphs ( rows ) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName is None for code , name , expected in [ ( "0042" , "empty" , "" ), ( "0043" , "equal" , "equal" ), ( "0044" , "explicit" , "OwnedProd" ), ]: assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( code ) . productionName == expected assert app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . productionName == expected assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "nil" ) . productionName == "nil"
title: Preserve nil, empty, equal and explicit values

text: Exact names, alternate names and accepted production aliases refer to the same represented record. A name read fills only a nil stored value. A raw handle obtained earlier observes that fill. copy and deepcopy retain independent production values from the time they were copied; neither is a live view of the later shared fill. from copy import copy , deepcopy with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "ownedLetter" , "unicode" : "0041" , "altNames" : "ownedAlias" , "script" : "latin" , "category" : "Letter" , }]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs raw = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) shallow , deep = copy ( raw ), deepcopy ( raw ) assert raw . productionName is None alias = app . glyphInfoForName ( "ownedAlias" ) assert ( alias . name , alias . productionName ) == ( "ownedLetter" , "ownedLetter" ) assert raw . productionName == "ownedLetter" assert shallow . productionName is None and deep . productionName is None
title: Observe shared fill and independent copies

text: A bare character that reaches Unicode lookup retains the raw shared record. A represented single-record uni or u name takes a copy, preserving its raw production at that time. Exact stored names still take priority over decoding. A direct Unicode miss can synthesize a record whose production is its constructed name. The name-factory fallback for a rejected scalar is a different route with a known nil value; these results do not qualify general complex-name synthesis. with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "ownedLetter" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" , }]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs raw = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) uni = app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041" ) u = app . glyphInfoForName ( "u0041" ) assert raw . productionName is None assert uni . productionName is None and u . productionName is None app . glyphInfoForName ( "ownedLetter" ) assert raw . productionName == "ownedLetter" assert uni . productionName is None and u . productionName is None synthesized = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0378" ) assert ( synthesized . name , synthesized . productionName ) == ( "uni0378" , "uni0378" ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "u10FFFF" ) . productionName is None
title: Distinguish Unicode text, uni/u copies and synthesized records

text: The manager's production helper computes an output; it does not rewrite an existing explicit raw field. Its represented rules are: Preserve nonempty explicit text, except a seven-UTF16-unit lowercase uni value with four-UTF16-unit Unicode produces uni plus that Unicode. For nil or empty helper input with Unicode, private-use encodings and Latin dotted/hyphenated names use uni or u plus the unchanged Unicode text. Other encoded names use the nice name. Without Unicode, remove hyphens and retain dots. If removal leaves empty text, retain the original name. Those helper rules do not override the getter's empty-value preservation. Derived suffix results expose the distinction. UTF16 units matter: a supplementary character occupies two units, unlike Python's scalar count. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "owned-ar" , "unicode" : "0627" , "production" : "uniFFFF" , "script" : "arabic" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "empty-latin" , "unicode" : "00C1" , "production" : "" , "script" : "latin" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "utf16" , "unicode" : "0041" , "production" : "uni😀xx" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "owned-name" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0627" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "owned-ar.ss01.alt" ) . productionName == "uni0627.ss01.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0627" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "empty-latin" ) . productionName == "" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "empty-latin.alt" ) . productionName == "uni00C1.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "utf16.alt" ) . productionName == "uni0041.alt" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName == "uni😀xx" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "owned-name" ) . productionName == "ownedname"
title: Keep normalization separate from the stored getter

text: The represented name lookup follows record order. Each record contributes its primary name, its production alias unless it starts with lowercase uni , and then alternate names. Later assignments win, even over an earlier primary name. The maintained public loader normalizes separator spaces in alternate names. Direct Unicode still selects its own stored record, even when that record's name has been shadowed in the name index. Lowercase uni exclusion applies to a production alias alone; it does not remove an exact stored primary name. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "earlier" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "later" , "production" : "earlier" , "altNames" : "First, Second" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "uni0041" , "production" : "Exact" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "excludedAlias" , "production" : "uni0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "earlier" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . name == "earlier" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) . productionName is None assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "First" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "Second" ) . name == "later" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041" ) . productionName == "Exact"
title: Preserve alias order and lowercase uni exclusions

text: Generic suffix output appends the exact remaining tokens to the base helper output. Repeated and empty suffix tokens are retained. A represented longer prefix takes priority over a shorter base; intermediate synthesized prefixes are not invented. Global lookup can fill the chosen shared base. The special case / cap context copies before its fill, preserving the earlier raw record. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "A.alt" , "unicode" : "0042" , "production" : "OwnedLongest" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A.alt.ss01..ss01" ) . productionName == "OwnedLongest.ss01..ss01" raw = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" ) assert raw . productionName is None cap = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A.cap" ) assert ( cap . case , cap . productionName ) == ( 1 , "A.cap" ) assert raw . productionName is None A represented canonical suffix after a uni/u copy has a separate boundary. When the last token is consumed, the copy retains the raw production of that canonical record. With tokens remaining, the helper computes their derived output. The canonical record's explicit raw value remains unchanged. with owned_glyphs ([ { "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }, { "name" : "A.alt" , "unicode" : "0042" , "unicodeLegacy" : "E001" , "production" : "uniFFFF" , "category" : "Letter" }, ]) as exports : app = exports . Glyphs consumed = app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041.alt" ) assert ( consumed . name , consumed . unicode , consumed . unicodeLegacy ) == ( "A.alt" , None , None ) assert consumed . productionName == "uniFFFF" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "uni0041.alt.ss01" ) . productionName == "uni0042.ss01" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0042" ) . productionName == "uniFFFF"
title: Retain suffix tokens and choose the represented longest prefix

text: A model's Glyph Info can share a global raw production field until a copy branch applies. An enabled stored metadata flag forces a copy even when its value is equal to the resolved value. The example uses an owned fake font backend; it does not qualify an actual FontLab edit, history step or saved font. from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend with owned_glyphs ([{ "name" : "A" , "unicode" : "0041" , "category" : "Letter" }]) as exports : app , Info = exports . text: Known nil metadata is different from metadata whose production source is unestablished. Classification inferred by a library does not establish a production value. The latter getter raises GSGlyphInfo.productionName.source ; do not replace that exception with a guessed None , empty string or sanitized export name. GSGlyphInfo ( SimpleNamespace ( name = "owned" , unicode = None , category = None , subCategory = None , script = None , case = 0 , )) try : value = unknown . productionName except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.productionName.source" else : raise AssertionError ( "An unavailable source must refuse" ) known = exports . Glyphs . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) try : known . productionName = "changed" except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.productionName" else : raise AssertionError ( "The snapshot must remain read-only" ) assert known . productionName == "A"

text: A partial projection allocates a plain SidebarItem , transfers selected fields through their setters and reparents the retained original children. It does not copy them. The original group still contains the same child whose parent now points to the projection. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) old = row ( p , "Original" , coverage = [ "A" ]) kept , removed = row ( p , "Kept" ), row ( p , "Removed" ) removed . setHidden_ ( True ) old . setSubItems_ ([ kept , removed ]) old . codes , old . badgeString , old . editable = [ "0041" ], "old badge" , True projected = manager . filterGroup_forFont_ ( old , OwnedFont ( p )) assert type ( projected ) is SidebarItem and projected is not old assert projected . subItems == [ kept ] and projected . subItems [ 0 ] is kept assert old . subItems == [ kept , removed ] assert kept . parent is projected and removed . parent is old assert projected . coverage is old . coverage assert projected . codes is None and projected . badgeString is None assert projected . editable is False and projected . isCalculating () assert p . events [ - 1 ] == ( "schedule" , 10_000_000 ) drain ( p . pending ) # No current font: update does no work and calculating stays set. assert projected . isCalculating () and not p . main

Order, categories and current resource reads

text: Category order follows the font's first encounters. Missing categories form the Other group, with an explicit NULL predicate. Only subcategories use the supplied comparison primitive. The mapping changes icon names; no mapping entry leaves the category name as the icon name. No native image is loaded here. p = SidebarPrimitives () manager , state = dynamic_manager ( p ) font = OwnedFont ( p , rows = [ SimpleNamespace ( category = "Mark" , subCategory = "Below" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = None , subCategory = "" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = "Mark" , subCategory = "Above" ), SimpleNamespace ( category = "Letter" , subCategory = None ), ]) groups = manager . categoriesFromFont_categoryToIconMapping_ ( font , { "Mark" : "OwnedIcon" }) assert [ g . identifier for g in groups ] == [ "Mark" , "Other" , "Letter" ] assert [ g . iconName for g in groups ] == [ "OwnedIcon" , "Other" , "Letter" ] assert [ g . identifier for g in groups [ 0 ] . subItems ] == [ "Below" , "Above" ] assert groups [ 0 ] . subItems [ 0 ] . parent is groups [ 0 ] assert groups [ 1 ] . predicate . predicateFormat == "category == NULL" assert groups [ 1 ] . subItems is None assert all ( g . cellType == "ImageTextCell" for g in groups )

text: The first receiver supplies default category overrides. Its dictionary object, including a nil result, becomes the process-once result. Later receivers and providers cannot refresh it merely by calling the method again. Mutations to that same returned dictionary remain visible. The isolated cache context keeps these experiments from contaminating other source examples. first , later = SidebarPrimitives (), SidebarPrimitives () first . mapping = { "Mark" : "base" , "Retained" : "keep" } first . category_rows = [{ "name" : "Mark" , "icon" : "override" }] later . mapping = { "Mark" : "later" } with fresh_category_cache (): with using_info_provider ( first ): mapping = GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () assert mapping is first . mapping assert mapping == { "Mark" : "override" , "Retained" : "keep" } mapping [ "OwnedNew" ] = "new" with using_info_provider ( later ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is mapping assert later . events == [] and mapping [ "OwnedNew" ] == "new" with fresh_category_cache (): first . mapping = None with using_info_provider ( first ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is None with using_info_provider ( later ): assert GSGlyphsInfo . categoryToIconMapping () is None

text: The builder reads fontType() twice and, for a nonempty first tag result, reads allTags again for coverage. It does not cache a final tree. These intentionally changing primitives make the repeated reads observable: the first type creates categories; the second type still includes languages. Tags take the second coverage object and schedule actual count work. text: The reload method replaces filter storage only after its actual loader returns. An exception leaves the old array in place. Successful processing still uses the persistent name map: duplicate identifiers do not replace the first map identity, although new filter rows are returned. Row insertion, copying and delayed work

text: Copying retains coverage and infos by identity while recursively copying children. Normal count values reset; the shallHaveCount == -2 sentinel preserves counts and badge. Bulk insertion outside the current array bounds inserts at zero. Removing a child removes duplicate occurrences but retains its old parent field. p = SidebarPrimitives () parent = row ( p , "Parent" , coverage = [ "A" ]) a , b , c = row ( p , "A" ), row ( p , "B" ), row ( p , "C" ) children = [ a ] parent . setSubItems_ ( children ) parent . insertObject_inSubItemsAtIndex_ ( b , 1 ) parent . insertSubItems_atIndex_ ([ c , b ], 100 ) assert parent . subItems is children and children == [ c , b , a , b ] parent . removeSubItemsObject_ ( b ) assert children == [ c , a ] and b . parent is parent parent . infos , parent . count , parent . shallHaveCount = [ record ( "A" )], 1 , 2 parent . badgeString = "1/2" duplicate = parent . copyWithZone_ ( None ) assert duplicate . coverage is parent . coverage and duplicate . infos is parent . infos assert duplicate . subItems [ 0 ] is not c and duplicate . subItems [ 0 ] . parent is duplicate assert c . parent is parent assert ( duplicate . count , duplicate . shallHaveCount , duplicate . badgeString ) == ( - 1 , - 1 , None ) parent . shallHaveCount = - 2 preserved = parent . copyWithZone_ ( None ) assert ( preserved . count , preserved . shallHaveCount , preserved . badgeString ) == ( 1 , - 2 , "1/2" ) nil_array = row ( p , "Nil array" ) nil_array . insertObject_inSubItemsAtIndex_ ( b , 500 ) assert nil_array . subItems is None and b . parent is nil_array
