text: Setting a font expands its current manager's name list and schedules a delayed count, then forwards to children. A second assignment while calculating changes the weak reference without adding a second count request. The scheduled body reads that current reference, so it counts the second font. A collected font becomes nil; nil-font count work does not clear calculating state. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Codes" ) item . codes = [ "0041" , "0042" ] first = OwnedFont ( p , label = "first" , codes = [ "0041" ]) second = OwnedFont ( p , label = "second" , codes = [ "0041" , "0042" ]) item . setFont_ ( first ) item . setFont_ ( second ) assert len ( p . pending ) == 1 and item . font is second drain ( p . pending ) assert ( "codes-count" , "second" ) in p . events assert item . count == - 1 and len ( p . main ) == 2 drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 2 , 2 , "✓" ) assert not item . isCalculating () item . setFont_ ( first ) del first gc . collect () assert item . font is None drain ( p . pending ) assert item . isCalculating () and not p . main
title: Resolve the weak font when the callback runs

text: Both range endpoints are looked up by name, then every code is looked up in the current Unicode index. Repeated rows remain repeated. A reversed range is consumed without output. Missing endpoint Unicode falls back to the whole name token and the new-record primitive. A nil record inside a valid range raises, preserving old infos and original coverage. p = SidebarPrimitives () a , b , c = record ( "A" , "0041" ), record ( "B" , "0042" ), record ( "C" , "0043" ) lookup = Lookup ({ "A" : a , "C" : c }, { "0041" : a , "0042" : b , "0043" : c }) item = row ( p , "Range" , coverage = [ "A:C" , "A" , "C:A" , "missing:end" ]) original = item . coverage item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert item . coverage is original assert item . infos [: 4 ] == [ a , b , c , a ] assert item . infos [ 4 ] . name == "missing:end" old = item . infos lookup . codes . pop ( "0042" ) item . coverage = [ "A:C" ] try : item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) except InfoNativeException as error : assert "range contains nil" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "A nil range member must fail" ) assert item . infos is old and item . coverage == [ "A:C" ]
title: Expand inclusive ranges without deduplicating

text: An ASCII-leading multi-unit alias with a different stored name is renamed. Locked records are copied first; unlocked records are renamed in place. These are explicit owned record fields, not inferred proprietary metadata. A malformed list member clears stored coverage and warns once per item name, but expansion continues over the original array. Later valid members are still included. p = SidebarPrimitives () locked , mutable = record ( "canonical" , locked = True ), record ( "mutable" ) lookup = Lookup ({ "Alias" : locked , "MutableAlias" : mutable }) item = row ( p , "Owned malformed list" , coverage = [ "Alias" , 123 , "MutableAlias" , "Alias" ]) item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert item . coverage is None assert [ r . name for r in item . infos ] == [ "Alias" , "MutableAlias" , "Alias" ] assert item . infos [ 0 ] is not locked and locked . name == "canonical" assert item . infos [ 1 ] is mutable and mutable . name == "MutableAlias" assert item . infos [ 2 ] is not item . infos [ 0 ] assert sum ( e [ 0 ] == "modal" for e in p . events ) == 1 item . coverage = [ False , "Alias" ] item . expandNameList_ ( lookup ) assert sum ( e [ 0 ] == "modal" for e in p . events ) == 1 assert len ( item . infos ) == 1 and item . infos [ 0 ] . name == "Alias"
title: Copy locked aliases and retain the original enumerator

text: Nonempty infos take precedence over predicate and codes. Expected count includes only infos with type zero. Calculation enqueues a working checkmark, then a publication callback. Until those callbacks run, stored count fields are unchanged. Only changed tuples emit hasShallHaveCount notifications. Repeating a successful publication still clears calculating and updates the badge. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Count" , predicate = p . compile_predicate ( "must not count" )) item . infos = [ record ( "A" ), record ( "B" , kind = 1 ), record ( "C" )] item . codes = [ "ignored" ] font = OwnedFont ( p , names = [ "A" , "C" ]) item . setIsCalculating_ ( True ) item . updateCount_ ( font ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( - 1 , - 1 , None ) assert len ( p . main ) == 2 and not any ( e [ 0 ] == "predicate-count" for e in p . events ) p . main . pop ( 0 )() assert item . badgeString == "✓" and item . count == - 1 p . main . pop ( 0 )() assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 2 , 2 , "✓" ) notifications = [ e for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] in ( "will" , "did" )] assert notifications == [( "will" , "hasShallHaveCount" , - 1 , - 1 ), ( "did" , "hasShallHaveCount" , 2 , 2 )] item . setIsCalculating_ ( True ) item . _publish_count ( 2 , 2 ) assert not item . isCalculating () assert [ e for e in p . events if e [ 0 ] in ( "will" , "did" )] == notifications
title: Separate calculation from main-thread publication

text: The exact case-two predicate supplies the expected source count; .sc lookup retains available records. The case-three predicate supplies the actual count. The resulting list is assigned to infos , while missingInfos remains intact. A marked exception in the second filter keeps the newly computed expected count but leaves old infos and the base count in place. Ordinary Python errors are not swallowed by this marked native-exception analogue. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Smallcaps" ) item . codes = [ "0041" ] sentinel = item . missingInfos = [ record ( "untouched" )] source_pattern = "(case == 2) AND NOT (name contains '.0') AND (export == True)" p . filtered [ source_pattern ] = [ record ( "a" ), record ( "b" )] p . filtered [ "case == 3" ] = [ record ( "a.sc" )] sc = record ( "a.sc" ) font = OwnedFont ( p , manager = Lookup ({ "a.sc" : sc }), names = [ "a.sc" ], codes = [ "0041" ]) item . updateCount_ ( font ) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( 1 , 2 , "1/2" ) assert item . infos == [ sc ] and item . infos [ 0 ] is sc assert item . missingInfos is sentinel old_infos = item . infos p . filtered [ "case == 3" ] = InfoNativeException ( "owned second filter failure" ) item . updateCount_ ( font ) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount ) == ( 1 , 2 ) assert item . infos is old_infos and item . missingInfos is sentinel assert any ( e [ 0 ] == "log" and "second filter failure" in e [ 1 ] for e in p . events ) assert old_infos == [ sc ]
title: Follow Smallcaps success and partial failure

text: Calling this selector is an explicit source experiment. Python does not invoke Objective-C automatic class initialization. For five active processors, the retained float32 half-count and nearest-away rounding yield three workers, with QoS 17. A second call retains the first queue object. This queue is independent of a manager's queue and does not itself replace the delayed scheduler primitive. from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import info_sidebar_support class CountQueue : def setMaxConcurrentOperationCount_ ( self , count ): self . limit = count def setQualityOfService_ ( self , quality ): self . quality = quality p = SidebarPrimitives () queue = CountQueue () allocations = [] def new_queue (): allocations . append ( queue ) return queue p . new_queue = new_queue p . active_processor_count = lambda : 5 saved = info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized , info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue try : info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized = False info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue = None with using_info_provider ( p ): SidebarItem . initialize () SidebarItem . initialize () assert allocations == [ queue ] assert ( queue . limit , queue . quality ) == ( 3 , 17 ) assert info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue is queue finally : ( info_sidebar_support . _queue_initialized , info_sidebar_support . _sidebar_queue ) = saved
title: Initialize the independent sidebar queue explicitly

text: The format setter catches only marked compilation failures, queues an alert and retains the previous predicate. It does not assign predicateFormat , create the constructor's fallback predicate or force a stop badge. Marked count failures instead report error 992 and publish (-2, -2) . They deduplicate by the current predicate format; an ordinary error still propagates before publication. p = SidebarPrimitives () item = row ( p , "Owned count failure" ) item . setPredicateFormat_ ( "owned prior" ) prior = item . predicate item . setPredicateFormat_ ( "owned bad filter" ) assert item . predicate is prior and item . predicateFormat is None assert item . count == - 1 and len ( p . main ) == 1 drain ( p . main ) assert p . events [ - 1 ] == ( "alert" , "owned compilation failure" ) p . predicate_counts [ "owned prior" ] = InfoNativeException ( "owned count failure" ) item . updateCount_ ( OwnedFont ( p )) drain ( p . main ) assert ( item . count , item . shallHaveCount , item . badgeString ) == ( - 2 , - 2 , None ) assert ( "error" , 992 ) in p . events p . predicate_counts [ "owned prior" ] = ValueError ( "ordinary error" ) try : item . updateCount_ ( OwnedFont ( p )) except ValueError as error : assert str ( error ) == "ordinary error" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unmarked errors must propagate" ) assert len ( p . main ) == 1 # The working badge was already queued before failure. drain ( p . main )
title: Keep compilation and count errors distinct

text: The document calls its file primitives rather than treating a path string as an NSDocument. The following setup supplies URL selectors and a superclass file setter only. Optional observer methods on the owned subclass record their order; they do not watch the filesystem. All font data lives in a temporary owned tree. class OwnedURL : def __init__ ( self , name , parent = None ): self . name , self . parent = name , parent def path ( self ): return self . name def URLByDeletingLastPathComponent ( self ): return self . parent def isEqual_ ( self , other ): return isinstance ( other , OwnedURL ) and self . name == other . name class FilePrimitives : def __init__ ( self , url , kind = "com.schriftgestaltung.glyphs" ): self . url , self . kind , self . events = url , kind , [] def file_url ( self , document ): return self . url def set_file_url ( self , document , url ): self . events . append ( "super-set-url" ) self . url = url def file_type ( self , document ): return self . kind class OwnedDocument ( GSDocument ): def stopObservingFile ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "stop" ) def startObservingFile ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "start" ) def updateFileObservers ( self ): self . _file_primitives . events . append ( "update" )
title: Documents: real local loading and explicit missing adapters

text: The document computes the parent URL before entering its manager lock. It keeps the old local manager until the new initializer returns. This example runs the actual sidebar initialization, local XML parsing, shared-manager fallback and queue drain through the earlier complete lifecycle fixture. The first load's temporary rows are real parsed invented data, rather than a fabricated manager return. An equal URL calls only the superclass setter; a changed URL calls stop, superclass setter, conditional start, update and then actual loading. The new invalid XML experiment keeps the source's non-atomic loaded state and reported error; it does not invent an exception or rollback. with owned_lifecycle () as ( provider , folder_url , data ): font = OwnedFont ( SidebarPrimitives (), types = ( 0 , 0 , 0 )) file_url = OwnedURL ( str ( data . parent / "Owned.glyphs" ), folder_url ) document = OwnedDocument ( font ) files = document . _file_primitives = FilePrimitives ( file_url ) assert document . loadCustomGlyphsData () is True local = document . glyphsInfo () assert local . _lifecycle . localURL is folder_url assert local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "owned.local" ) . unicode == "0042" assert local . allItem () . identifier == "All" assert local . categoriesGroup () . subItems [ 0 ] . identifier == "Owned" assert not local . _lifecycle . queue . pending assert document . valueForKey_ ( "glyphsInfo" ) is local document . setFileURL_ ( OwnedURL ( file_url . name , folder_url )) assert files . events == [ "super-set-url" ] and document . glyphsInfo () is local changed = OwnedURL ( str ( data . parent / "Other.glyphs" ), folder_url ) document . setFileURL_ ( changed ) assert files . events == [ "super-set-url" , "stop" , "super-set-url" , "start" , "update" ] replacement = document . glyphsInfo () assert replacement is not local assert replacement . glyphInfoForName_ ( "owned.local" ) . unicode == "0042" data . write_text ( "<glyph broken" , encoding = "utf-8" ) assert document . loadCustomGlyphsData () is True assert document . glyphsInfo () is not replacement assert any ( event [ 0 ] == "error" for event in provider . events ) files . url = None assert document . loadCustomGlyphsData () is True assert document . _local_glyph_info is None
title: Load the parent folder through the actual constructor

text: The four monitored types are Glyphs, UFO, Glyphs package and icon set. Other types do not start an observer. Missing observer selectors take the source's optional branches; that does not install a monitor. Missing file primitives refuse. Likewise the current FontLab GSFont has no qualified fontType() mapping for these algorithms: ordinary model access must not silently assume type zero. manager , canonical = owned_manager () exports , font = owned_exports ( manager ) assert type ( font . parent ) is GSDocument document = GSDocument ( font ) assert document . shouldMonitorFile_ ( "com.schriftgestaltung.glyphs" ) assert document . shouldMonitorFile_ ( "org.unifiedfontobject.ufo" ) assert document . shouldMonitorFile_ ( "com.glyphsapp.glyphspackage" ) assert document . shouldMonitorFile_ ( "com.glyphsapp.iconset" ) assert not document . shouldMonitorFile_ ( "owned.unmonitored" ) try : document . loadCustomGlyphsData () except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert "fileURL" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "An unqualified document URL must refuse" ) document . _file_primitives = FilePrimitives ( None , "owned.unmonitored" ) assert document . loadCustomGlyphsData () is True try : font . fontType () except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert "fontType" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "FontLab fontType needs a qualified adapter" )
title: Refuse unqualified file and font-type dependencies

text: These are source-contract experiments, not native FontLab acceptance. A usable FontLab adapter must qualify GSFont.fontType , lock/KVC/current glyph collection access, file URL/type/superclass setter behavior and file observers. Sidebar defaults, real predicate compilation/evaluation, lawful category/filter/icon resources, image lookup, localization, record fields and count operations also need concrete adapters. Scheduling must execute the real callbacks with the appropriate queue/main-thread semantics; recording callback counts alone does not complete that work. Python weak references, locks and lists do not prove Cocoa weak references, NSArray mutation/zone behavior, KVO delivery or process-once exception behavior. Explicit SidebarItem.initialize() is separate from Objective-C automatic class initialization. The owned nil-array policy above must never become an assertion that every native array accepts nil. Projection and count failures retain the source's partial state; a cleanup or rollback policy needs its own evidence. The reusable verification runner executes every tagged experiment from a fresh namespace with the exact published setup. It also runs the prior 99 active examples independently and checks loaded provider origins. Installed mode allows no source override and requires the active ordinary installation prefix. Matching wheel/sdist payloads, complete consumers, actual FontLab behavior, original font workflows, generated reference/rendered pages and publication remain separate acceptance steps. The retained native/UI examples remain held and unchanged.
title: Carry the result to a real integration

text: Use Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode(string_or_int, font=None) in the default Glyphs4 profile. Glyphs2/3 use String instead. The current private candidate returns the selected manager's read-only GSGlyphInfo view or None ; omitting font selects shared metadata without reading the active font. Its maintained GlyphData index includes primary and legacy encodings. The returned record keeps those fields separate; lookup does not assign either encoding to a glyph or run font-local postprocessing. The manager/profile guide supplies current runnable replacements. The examples below now select their intended profiles explicitly, use real font-manager delegation and distinguish unknown public recipes from finalized owned recipes. Run its owned graph setup first for the owned_application and owned_parsed_manager fixtures. Original predecessor bodies remain preserved in external verification evidence. These eight examples use owned offline application fixtures and the linked setup. They import actual package exports without activating a synthetic GlyphsApp module, opening FontLab or executing an original script. At the earlier named checkpoint, all 24 retained examples and 11 then-new production examples passed in both ordinary six-wheel prefixes, with installed module origins checked and all 702 runtime/data files matching byte for byte. Echopy producer provenance matches the corrected Glyport source; exact artifact identities and consumer results are on the existing Glyport package page linked below. These offline checks do not qualify a published release or native workflow.
title: Global Unicode Glyph Info

text: Glyphs2/3 bind String , with a capital S; Glyphs4 binds string_or_int . The human-readable label Unicode is not a keyword alias. Missing/unknown/ duplicate arguments fail at Python binding before lookup. Current indexed records retain canonical record views. Public NFD does not establish a physical metadata recipe; an unknown components source now refuses instead of publishing NFD as that recipe. The example checks that public refusal, then verifies a known owned recipe. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication , GSGlyphInfo app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = None )) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( String = "004a" , font = None ) . name == "J" info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "00C1" ) assert isinstance ( info , GSGlyphInfo ) and info . name == "Aacute" try : _ = info . components except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyphInfo.components.source" else : raise AssertionError ( "Public NFD does not establish a physical recipe" ) manager = owned_parsed_manager () manager . updateComponentsInfos () info = manager . infoFromDataForUnicode_ ( "00C1" ) assert [ part . name for part in info . components ] == [ "A" , "acutecomb" ] assert all ( isinstance ( part , GSGlyphInfo ) for part in info . components ) info . components . clear () assert [ part . name for part in info . components ] == [ "A" , "acutecomb" ] try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( Unicode = "0041" ) except TypeError : pass else : raise AssertionError ( "Unicode is not the executable keyword" ) Current known component records are shallow references in independent returned lists. Explicit custom finalization shows an established recipe without inferring one from an encoding or outline.
title: Call the executable keyword

text: Glyphs3 tests isinstance(String, int) and applies exactly "%04X" % String ; Glyphs2 uses an exact-int test. Glyphs4 uses isinstance and f-string 04X formatting, including subclass __format__ . Four is a minimum width and does not validate scalar range. The example selects the real Glyphs3 profile to retain its percent-formatting assertions. The new guide also exercises Glyphs2 and Glyphs4. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class OwnedInt ( int ): def __int__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not coerce an integer subclass" ) def __format__ ( self , specification ): raise AssertionError ( "Preserve percent formatting" ) app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = None )) for value , spelling in [( 65 , "0041" ), ( OwnedInt ( 65 ), "0041" ), ( True , "0001" ), ( False , "0000" ), ( - 1 , "-001" )]: actual = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) expected = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( spelling ) assert ( actual . name , actual . unicode ) == ( expected . name , expected . unicode ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( OwnedInt ( 65 )) . name == "A" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( - 1 ) . name == "uni-001" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( 0x10FFFF ) is None
title: Preserve integer formatting

text: Glyphs2/3 integer Name dispatch calls the instance Unicode method without a font keyword. Glyphs4 passes font=font , including None, through the instance method. An explicit-font string Name query selects that font's manager in all three profiles. The former unconditional .localData refusal is superseded; a selected manager's actual result/error now propagates. The explicit Glyphs3 example below retains its integer/override contract while checking real string-name font delegation and its access-error propagation. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class UnreadableFont : def __getattribute__ ( self , name ): raise AssertionError ( "Global lookup must not read the active font" ) active = UnreadableFont () app = owned_application ( "glyphs3" , SimpleNamespace ( font = active )) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( 65 , font = active ) . name == "A" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" , font = None ) . name == "A" local = owned_parsed_manager () explicit = SimpleNamespace ( glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = explicit ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "A" ) try : app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = active ) except AssertionError as error : assert str ( error ) == "Global lookup must not read the active font" else : raise AssertionError ( "Explicit font access errors must propagate" ) calls = [] class OwnedApplication ( type ( app )): def glyphInfoForUnicode ( self , * args , ** kwargs ): calls . append (( args , kwargs )) return "owned override" owned = OwnedApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = active ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert owned . glyphInfoForName ( True , font = active ) == "owned override" assert calls == [(( True ,), {})] Both global routes ignore active-font glyph state, parameters, ROS and stored overrides. They do not invoke the per-glyph metadata postprocessing pipeline. A result of None does not trigger a search of font.glyphs .
title: Glyphs2/3 integer name lookup discards the font first

text: Integer formatting occurs before selecting an explicit font manager. Only None selects shared; a false-valued font still receives glyphsInfo() . There is no unconditional .localData refusal. A malformed object used as a font can fail at its own method access. With the default manager, built-in strings and None remain supported after profile-specific integer dispatch; unqualified bridge payload types retain .inputType refusal. The example exercises conversion and selected-manager identity before default manager payload checks; it does not manufacture a blanket local-data refusal. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication class NoCoercion : def __str__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not stringify bridge inputs" ) def __index__ ( self ): raise AssertionError ( "Do not coerce bridge inputs to integers" ) class OwnedString ( str ): pass app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) class Recorder : def glyphInfoForUnicode_ ( self , value ): return value class ExplicitFont : def glyphsInfo ( self ): return Recorder () def __bool__ ( self ): return False for value in ( None , [], 65 , True , "" , " \ud800 00" ): actual = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value , font = ExplicitFont ()) if isinstance ( value , int ): assert actual == f " { value : 04X } " else : assert actual is value try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0041" , font = False ) except AttributeError as error : assert "glyphsInfo" in str ( error ) else : raise AssertionError ( "False is an explicit font object, not omitted font" ) for value in ( 65.0 , b "0041" , [], NoCoercion (), OwnedString ( "0041" )): try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.inputType" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unqualified bridge inputs must refuse" )
title: Respect refusal precedence

text: After the original-length gate, the uppercase text is the exact Unicode-index key. There is no trimming, zero padding, prefix removal or numeric canonicalization. Thus 004a selects J , while 041 and 000041 miss 0041 and synthesize their own raw names. Each source record contributes its primary encodings, then its non-nil legacy encoding to the same index, in record/file order; the last assignment wins. The parser/loader contract and retained ARM instructions establish this ordering, rather than a new native run. The pinned public glyphsLib 6.16.2 GlyphData snapshot has 74,247 records and 71,401 primary keys. Its 730 distinct legacy keys produce 72,131 combined keys, with no overlap or change to existing primary entries in this snapshot. The duplicated legacy key 0000 belongs first to .null , then to NULL ; lookup selects NULL . FE8D selects alef-ar.isol , and FE80 selects hamza-ar.isol . Their primary Unicode remains None ; a legacy hit never promotes its key into that field. These public counts do not establish proprietary database completeness or the same record set in every resource/version. Synthesis applies only after a true combined-index miss. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "004a" ) . name == "J" for text , name in [( "041" , "uni041" ), ( "000041" , "uni000041" )]: info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , text , None ) for text , name , primary , legacy in [ ( "FE8D" , "alef-ar.isol" , None , "FE8D" ), ( "FE80" , "hamza-ar.isol" , None , "FE80" ), ( "0000" , "NULL" , None , "0000" ), ]: info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . name , info . unicode , info . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) named = app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) assert ( named . name , named . unicode , named . unicodeLegacy ) == ( name , primary , legacy ) assert info is named # Canonical views of the same selected raw record. assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "fe8d" ) . name == "alef-ar.isol" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "U+0041" ) is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "0x41" ) is None
title: Exact combined-index lookup precedes raw synthesis

text: None and text shorter than three UTF-16 code units return None before uppercasing, lookup or parsing. Count UTF-16 units rather than Python code points: a supplementary scalar occupies two. An uppercase expansion cannot rescue a too-short input. 0ﬀ returns None; 00ﬀ becomes 00FF and selects ydieresis ; 000ﬀ becomes 000FF and synthesizes. Actual malformed UTF16 and hex text naming a surrogate are different domains. After the minimum-length gate, malformed actual UTF16 refuses with .UTF16 : Foundation can return a NULL UTF8 pointer that the retained upstream helper would dereference unchecked. Do not execute that native failure path. A shorter lone surrogate returns None at the earlier length gate; valid surrogate pairs are not rejected as malformed. Literal ASCII D800 is accepted synthesis text. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for value in ( None , "" , "0" , "00" , "0ﬀ" , " \ud800 " , " \ud800 0" , "😀0" , " \ud83d\ude00 0" ): assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "00ﬀ" ) . name == "ydieresis" assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "000ﬀ" ) . name == "uni000FF" for value in ( " \ud800 00" , "00 \ud800 " , " \udc00 00" ): try : app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.UTF16" else : raise AssertionError ( "Unsafe malformed UTF16 must refuse" ) assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "D800" ) . unicode == "D800" Standalone macOS 27.2 Foundation calibration checked all 1,112,064 valid Unicode scalars against Python 3.11 Unicode 14 uppercasing. There were 55 differences; only non-ASCII ﬀ uppercased entirely into the parser alphabet, identically in both systems. That establishes this measured parser-alphabet boundary. It does not establish arbitrary Foundation-version equivalence, PyObjC conversion or native font-workflow compatibility.
title: Check original UTF16 length before uppercase expansion

text: On a combined-index miss, the retained helper scans ASCII hex in reverse. Spaces contribute nothing; any minus sign requests final negation, regardless of its position, and repeated minuses do not toggle the sign. Both are skipped without advancing the nibble position. Other characters return sentinel 0x7FFFFFFF , which fails the manager’s range check. Nonempty spaces/minuses alone parse as zero. Nibble contributions are added modulo 2³² with shifts (4 * position) & 31 . This differs from parsing an unlimited integer and truncating it: 100000000 parses as 1 and FFFFFFFFF as 14. Signed values below 0x10000 use the uni prefix; other accepted values use u . Signed high-bit patterns take the BMP branch and bypass its upper-range guard. On the other branch, 10FFFE passes but 10FFFF fails. This is not a strict Unicode scalar validator. Names use that prefix plus the uppercase original text , not a reformatted parsed integer. The synthesized primary encoding preserves the same text only when its uppercase UTF16 length is 1–7. A longer valid record has unicode=None . No encoding is assigned to a font by reading one of these snapshots. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for text in ( "--41" , "04-1" , " 4 1 " , " " , "---" ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert info . name == "uni" + text and info . unicode == text for text in ( "00000041" , "80000000" , "FFFFFFFF" , "100000000" , "FFFFFFFFF" ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert info . name == "uni" + text and info . unicode is None assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( "10FFFE" ) . name == "u10FFFE" for text in ( "10FFFF" , "110000" , "7FFFFFFF" , "nothex" ): assert app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) is None
title: Preserve the historical parser and raw encoding

text: Synthesized case is 0; subCategory and unicodeLegacy are None. Private Use gets category Private Use and no script in exactly E000–F8FF, F0000–FFFFD and 100000–10FFFD. Otherwise the audited historical Han set gives script han and category Letter ; other synthesized records have script None and category Other . Surrogate hex text, unassigned points, controls, punctuation and noncharacters are not generally filtered out. Direct indexed entries retain their maintained metadata and can mask these synthesis rules. The Han intervals are the following hexadecimal start/count pairs; each covers [start, start + count) . They describe retained source, not current Unicode Script data: Start Count Start Count 2E80 1A 2E9B 59 2F00 D6 3005 1 3007 1 3021 9 3038 3 303B 1 3400 19B6 4E00 51CD F900 16E FA70 6A 2F800 21E 20000 A6D7 2A700 1035 2B740 DE 2B820 1682 2CEB0 1D31 30000 134B 1F200 100 The seven-digit spellings below force a combined-index miss so the historical classification can be observed independently of canonical maintained entries. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp import GSApplication app = GSApplication ( SimpleNamespace ( font = None ), object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) for value , script , category in [( 0x9FCC , "han" , "Letter" ), ( 0x9FCD , None , "Other" ), ( 0x3134A , "han" , "Letter" ), ( 0x3134B , None , "Other" ), ( 0xF8FF , None , "Private Use" )]: text = " %07X " % value info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( text ) assert ( info . script , info . category ) == ( script , category ) assert info . unicode == text and info . case == 0 assert info . subCategory is None and info . unicodeLegacy is None for value in ( 0xE000 , 0xF0000 , 0xFFFFD , 0x100000 , 0x10FFFD ): info = app . glyphInfoForUnicode ( value ) assert info . category == "Private Use" and info . script is None
title: Classify synthesis using historical ranges

text: Supported snapshot fields here are name, primary Unicode, separate legacy Unicode, category, subCategory, script, case and supported component snapshots. A synthesized record’s minimal fields do not qualify every Glyph Info property. Maintained glyphsLib data is not proof of Glyphs’ proprietary database completeness, the same record contents or Unicode version. Source-supported index ordering alone does not qualify custom resource loading or replacement. The stored production guide now describes the bounded represented-record source contract; it remains separate from glyph production write/export and application conversion. The retained production successor passes both ordinary prefixes and the exact consumer checks; the checkpoint suffix-route correction has separate source/archive evidence. The compound guide now covers raw/shared/copy state and multi-record composition; its new ordinary provider/consumer cohort remains pending. Private global overlays, font-local managers, remaining fields and arbitrary bridge conversion remain unimplemented or unqualified. See legacy Unicode and ROS for legacy snapshots and the proprietary ROS mapping refusal, parameters and Arabic encodings for ordered font-local postprocessing, and the Glyport package for the broader compatibility surface. Whole original scripts, native collisions, history and saved/reopened workflows remain separate acceptance work. The source-lock review, generated reference/site, archive/routes, browser/accessibility and publication gates remain open; this authored candidate does not clear them.
title: Keep acceptance boundaries explicit

text: Use the reviewed wheel or source distribution from each package's GitHub release. Private repositories require authenticated access. Keep credentials in your normal GitHub tooling; never put them in documentation, URLs or Python scripts.
title: Install and connect

text: Install Instamix 1.0.9 or newer first. Download its standalone install.vfpy , then open that file in FontLab. It bootstraps the stdlib-only installer from a validated wheel; a pre-existing pip or venv is not required. The current generated project installer checks migration and rollback capabilities before reusing its provider. Do not use Instamix 1.0.8 to upgrade an old install.vfpy installation: a failed replacement could remove other files recorded by that legacy installer. In FontLab's Scripting panel, install ordinary distribution requirements with: from fontlab_instamix import install_packages install_packages ( "uharfbuzz>=0.57" ) Instamix finds or downloads uv, verifies a standalone Python matching the target, and creates or checks the shared venv. Packages go to <data>/python/<major.minor>/site-packages , which FontLab already reads. The venv reads that same directory through its own managed .pth ; FontLab does not need to process that file. An incompatible existing venv is refused rather than replaced. Installation refreshes import caches, without reloading imported modules. For a source project with [tool.fontlab-install] , open its current install.vfpy . For a ready .fontlabext , .fontlabextz or root manifest, use the Instamix extension API . Its records and uninstall commands are under Scripts > Instamix . Default data-folder discovery uses an explicit argument, then FONTLAB_DATA_DIR , then native preferences' dataPathDefault , then the platform default. A custom current application dataPath is a different value: pass the intended folder explicitly when those differ. Never assume a terminal's Python version or architecture matches the running FontLab.
title: Install inside FontLab

text: Install external clients such as Remopy into an ordinary environment with uv pip install PATH_TO_WHEEL . That environment does not make packages available to embedded FontLab. Instamix explains explicit targets and the external CLI. FontLab supplies its native bindings and existing Qt application; install neither PySide binaries nor a second Qt application into that host.
title: Install outside FontLab

text: App 1.2.31, Plugmix 1.1.19 and Remopy 2.0.7 have checked GitHub release artifacts, but their PyPI uploads failed because trusted publishers were not configured. Do not lower a dependency floor to work around a missing release. Use the checked release-wheel download URLs with uv pip install in an ordinary Python environment. The App and Plugmix versions above resolved together in a fresh ordinary arm64 Python 3.11 environment. That is an ordinary package-install check, not a FontLab plugin deployment test. Use the reviewed source installer or extension pack for its Scripts and bundles. Recheck publication status when choosing later releases; keep version floors and artifact identity aligned. Instamix 1.0.9 or newer is still needed for legacy project upgrades. The captured API uses FontLab9, Python3.11 and Qt5. The source-only documentation environment uses Python3.12 or newer. A PySide2 binary wheel is a reference input; it is not loaded into FontLab's PythonQt runtime.
title: Temporary release inputs

text: FontLab 9.1.9813 bridge defect The native MCP bridge can crash in BridgeConnection::updateTimeout on this build ( fontlab/fl#8657 ). Remopy setup/tools/run and Instamix --remote can time out. A submitted operation's outcome is unknown until its receipt is checked. Do not retry automatically. Until a fixed bridge ships, run an owned .vfpy directly through FontLab's File > Open and have it write a result file; submission alone proves no work. On a build with a working MCP bridge, enable FontLab's MCP server, then connect: from fontlab_remopy import FontLab with FontLab () as app : print ( app . fonts ()) print ( app . output ()) eval() returns a JSON-native value. run() captures stdout/stderr and a result; bind variables as keyword arguments rather than interpolating them into code. The native execution deadline still applies. A timeout can leave an operation's outcome unknown, so mutating calls are never retried automatically. with FontLab () as app : answer = app . eval ( "value + 2" , value = 40 ) execution = app . run ( "print(message) \n result = 42" , message = "Hello, FontLab" ) For asynchronous programs, use AsyncFontLab with async with and await calls.
title: Connect from another process

text: FontLab 9 lets Python draw on the Glyph canvas and register its own tools. Both hooks live on the host objects, so you need no helper package to use them. Plugmix and Glyport wrap them with friendlier APIs. Host build These methods exist only in FontLab 9 builds that include the Python scripting hooks. Check hasattr(flCanvas, "appendPythonPainter") before relying on them. Everything here runs on the GUI thread. Calling a registration function from another thread raises RuntimeError .
title: Native Python hooks in FontLab 9

text: from fontlab import flWorkspace canvas = flWorkspace . instance () . getActiveCanvas () # a flCanvas, or nothing getActiveCanvas() returns the canvas of the active window, or nothing when no canvas is active.
title: Get the canvas

text: from fontlab import flCanvas from PythonQt import QtCore , QtGui def paint ( painter , canvas ): painter . setPen ( QtGui . QColor ( "#d03030" )) centre = canvas . mapToViewportF ( QtCore . QPointF ( 0 , 0 )) painter . drawEllipse ( centre , 8 , 8 ) token = canvas . appendPythonPainter ( paint , flCanvas . OverOwner ) # later canvas . removePythonPainter ( token ) appendPythonPainter(callback, order=UnderOwner) returns an integer token. removePythonPainter(token) returns True when it removed the painter and False when the token is unknown or belongs to another canvas. Callback signature. callback(painter, canvas) . The painter is a QPainter ; the canvas is the flCanvas being painted. Order. flCanvas.UnderOwner ( 0 ) paints before the item that owns the canvas (the glyph); flCanvas.OverOwner ( 1 ) paints after it. Any other value raises ValueError . The default is UnderOwner . Coordinates. FontLab resets the painter's transform before each call, so you draw in viewport pixels, with the origin at the viewport's top-left corner. To place something at a canvas position, convert it first: mapToViewportF takes a QPointF and returns a QPointF , or takes a QLineF and returns a QLineF . mapToViewport is the integer form for QPoint , QRectF and QPolygonF . Pen widths and text sizes stay in pixels, so they do not scale with zoom. Painter lifetime. The painter is valid only during the callback. Do not store it, and do not use it after the callback returns. FontLab saves the painter state before calling you and restores it afterwards. Errors. An exception in your callback is printed to the Python console and does not stop the paint. Other painters still run. Scope and cleanup. A painter belongs to one canvas, and FontLab discards it when that canvas is destroyed. Painting does not nest: a callback that provokes another paint pass during painting is skipped for that pass. Adding or removing a painter asks the canvas to repaint.
title: Draw with a canvas painter

text: from fontlab import flWorkspace class Probe : def activate ( self ): print ( "probe on" ) def deactivate ( self ): print ( "probe off" ) def mousePressed ( self , event , canvas ): print ( event . pos ()) return True # handled def paint ( self , painter , canvas ): painter . drawText ( 10 , 20 , "Probe" ) workspace = flWorkspace . instance () token = workspace . registerPythonTool ( "Probe" , None , Probe ()) # later workspace . unregisterPythonTool ( token ) registerPythonTool(name, icon, object) returns an integer token. name must not be empty. icon is a QIcon or None . object is any Python object; FontLab looks up each method by name when the event happens, so implement only what you need. The tool appears as a checkable action in the Tools list and in the toolbar. unregisterPythonTool(token) removes those entries, deactivates the tool if it is active, and returns True on success. Method Arguments Called when activate , deactivate none The tool becomes, or stops being, the main tool. mousePressed , mouseMoved , mouseReleased , mouseDoubleClicked (event, canvas) A mouse event reaches a canvas of the tool's workspace. keyPressed , keyReleased (event, canvas) A key event reaches such a canvas. paint (painter, canvas) The canvas paints over the owner. Same rules as a canvas painter. Events. Mouse methods receive a QMouseEvent , key methods a QKeyEvent . Both are valid only during the call. Return a true value to mark the event as handled; FontLab then accepts it and stops normal processing. Return nothing to let FontLab continue. FontLab offers a key press to keyPressed before it resolves shortcuts, so a handled key beats a shortcut, and it reuses your answer for the key press that follows. Active tool only. Event methods and paint run only while your tool is the active tool. paint always runs over the owner. Cleanup. FontLab unregisters a workspace's tools when that workspace closes. A callback may safely unregister its own tool.
title: Register a tool

text: Need Hook An overlay that is always on, in every tool Canvas painter An overlay or interaction that belongs to one tool Tool paint and mouse methods A menu or toolbar entry that takes over the canvas Tool For ready-made reporters, filters and tools see Plugmix ; Glyport uses the same hooks for Glyphs reporters and tools. Fontlabapp's glyph_window.draw overlay is a separate mechanism, not a wrapper for these hooks; see Fontlabapp .
title: Choosing between the hooks

text: Inside FontLab, echopy.fontlab delegates to the original fontlab objects; echopy.fontgate and echopy.fontpr follow the same contract. from echopy import fontlab as fl font = fl . CurrentFont () glyph = fl . CurrentGlyph () node = fl . flNode ( 120 , 340 ) Use flNode and the complete class member indexes to inspect captured signatures and enriched documentation. Any and variadic arguments mark incomplete native signature information. They are not permission to pass arbitrary objects; confirm an uncertain operation against the running host. The native modules have their own top-level Native API section in the navigation: fontlab , fontgate , fontpr , FL and PythonQt . Each module page starts with an overview and tables of its functions, classes and constants.
title: Native scripting

text: Fly provides nine lazy module aliases: Alias Target fly.fl echopy.fontlab fly.fg echopy.fontgate fly.tr typerig fly.pr echopy.fontpr fly.qt native PythonQt fly.ap fontlabapp fly.qs pythonqtside fly.gp fontlab_glyport fly.fp fontlab_fontport They share the canonical module objects. Documentation names use the live API's natural namespaces, while source and enrichment hashes retain provenance. Outside FontLab, native construction and operations fail with NativeUnavailable . Documentation builds read source and stubs without invoking these operations.
title: Short imports

text: These examples use the ordinary development App package 0.2.26.dev159+gb1e905b61 . Older versions can clear and rebuild the selection even with add=True . The examples below were checked against the installed artifact with owned native doubles; their FontLab behavior remains unqualified.
title: Read and extend the Font-window selection

text: Keep the two native identifiers separate. package.id binds App operations to a package; package.fgId identifies the FontGate carrier used by the legacy selection reader. The reader returns selected glyph names in font order. It is not a list of every displayed glyph, nor a record of selected chart cells: one glyph can occur in several cells. Defining this function does not access FontLab. Calling it reads selection and returns the package identifier with the names. A two-second deadline bounds the Python scan, but cannot interrupt a blocking native call. The final identity check rejects a font switch; it does not prove an atomic snapshot if native state changes and changes back during the scan. from time import monotonic from fontlabapp.core.scripting import current_package , names_font_window_selection def read_font_selection (): package = current_package () if package is None : raise ValueError ( "Open a font before reading its selection." ) package_id = int ( package . id ) names = names_font_window_selection ( expected_fg_id = int ( package . fgId ), deadline = monotonic () + 2.0 ) if current_package ( package_id ) is None : raise ValueError ( "The font changed during the selection read; run again." ) return package_id , names An empty selection is a valid empty list. This function does not fall back to the current Glyph-window glyph. Keep the returned package identifier with any report based on these names, so a later action cannot silently target another font.
title: Read names bound to one font

text: Pass the bound package identifier and the glyph names your report found to this function. Calling it changes the Font-window selection; it does not edit glyph outlines. Activate the regular Font window first. Readable selection data from a Glyph window does not make the legacy selection writers safe there. from fontlabapp.core.scripting import select_glyphs def add_report_names ( package_id , names ): selected = select_glyphs ( names , package_id = package_id , add = True ) print ( f "Selected { len ( selected ) } glyph names in total." ) return selected The helper validates every requested name before writing and rejects a stale package or unsupported active window. It adds only names that are not already selected, preserving the existing selection. Duplicate names do not cause repeated writes. Empty requests and already-selected names require no selection writes, but still undergo the package/window checks. The returned count is the total number of selected glyph names, not the number just added or the number of selected chart cells. An already-selected glyph's partial cell selection is left untouched. If a native addition fails, the exception propagates. Earlier additions can remain; this is not atomic rollback. Do not automatically retry, clear selection or apply a global Undo in an error handler. add=False is a different operation: it clears selection before selecting the requested names and does not have the same preservation behavior. Neither route calls UpdateAll() .
title: Add report results without clearing selection

text: Neither helper supplies the Font window's arranged, filtered cell list. A scan of all package glyphs or MCP list_glyphs with request filters is not equivalent to the current UI filter. The inspected C++ chart model has cell data, but its ordinary accessors are absent from the retained PythonQt capture. That bounded finding does not prove that every route is unavailable on every build. Before adapting a tool that operates on displayed cells, verify an exposed ordered snapshot with package-qualified glyph identities, duplicates and empty encoding cells. Define whether “visible” means included by the chart filter or inside the viewport. Test reads and writes on owned fonts, including font switches, filtered views and multiple cells for one glyph; source examples alone do not establish complete font, history or view-state preservation.
title: A displayed filter is a separate scope

text: A successful Python call does not prove that FontLab preserved every unrelated part of a font. Keep the returned counters and warnings, and qualify edits with Apply, Undo, Redo and saved-file reopen on owned copies before relying on a writer. Do not convert an exception into a success message or automatically repeat a failed edit: a partial write can already have changed the font. The examples below use the development App contract verified in ordinary package 0.2.26.dev158+g55fc09868 . This is a source/artifact checkpoint, not a published release or native acceptance claim. Older installed App versions may still refuse queued updates and may not accept the disclosure keyword.
title: Handle writer results and failures

text: FontLab can retain glyph IDs in its process-wide update queue after opening an editor or refreshing views. A later write may change those glyphs’ modification dates. Ordinary App writers disclose this as pending_updates and pending_note instead of refusing solely because the queue is nonempty. They do not clear the queue or restore unrelated dates to conceal the change. Field Meaning pending_updates Tuple of native glyph IDs captured before the write; these are not names or proof that those glyphs changed. pending_note Human-readable date caveat, or an empty string. undo_steps Raise Ascender’s completed changed occurrences, not a guarantee that a later Undo succeeded. nodes Raise Ascender’s counted node moves across its sequential occurrences. guides , layers Perpendicular Guides’ reported additions and affected-layer count. Use the stored note when formatting a result. Reading the native queue again can observe different state and lose the warning that applied to this action. from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note def raise_status ( result ): text = ( f "Moved { result [ 'nodes' ] } nodes across { result [ 'occurrences' ] } occurrences; " f " { result [ 'undo_steps' ] } Undo steps." ) return append_note ( text , result ) This formatter runs outside FontLab with an ordinary result dictionary. The helper appends a nonempty note once. A zero-move result is still a valid outcome: it does not mean every selected node required an edit.
title: Queued updates are a warning

text: Backend.execute() accepts an optional mutable disclosure dictionary. It resets the dictionary at entry and fills it before history, so a caller can display the queue warning even when no result is returned. A failure before queue sampling, or a no-op, leaves an empty disclosure; this does not prove that the native queue is empty. Without a dictionary, the backend prints the warning itself. This wrapper uses the formatter above. Defining it is safe outside FontLab; calling it requires FontLab and can change the current font. from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note from fontlabapp.contours.raise_ascender.native import Backend def raise_selected ( amount = "10" , * , all_layers = False ): disclosure = { "pending_updates" : (), "pending_note" : "" } try : result = Backend () . execute ( amount , all_layers , disclosure = disclosure ) except Exception as error : print ( append_note ( f "Raise Ascender failed: { error } " , disclosure )) raise print ( raise_status ( result )) return result all_layers=False uses the selected occurrences. True uses every foreground layer of the first selected glyph, including associated auxiliary layers; it is not an all-font operation. The writer retains its bound-font, source-change, automatic-dependent and history-scope checks. A queued-update warning does not waive any of those checks. On failure, the wrapper preserves the original exception and its Undo guidance. In a dialog, put the same formatted text in an owned status label instead of printing it. Keep the disclosure dictionary for that action only; do not reuse a previous action’s warning after a no-op or an early failure.
title: Preserve warnings when Raise Ascender fails

text: fontlabapp.guides.perpendicular.model.run() plans guides for the first selected layer. When the sampled queue is nonempty, it prints the warning before a possible append. On success it returns guides , layers , messages , pending_updates and pending_note . The warning is already printed; callers need not print it a second time. A no-op reports zero counts and empty disclosure without querying the queue. Source changes, automatic layers or affected automatic dependants still cause refusal. If an append partially fails, no success dictionary is returned. The warning has already been printed and the append-failure exception directs the user to inspect Edit > Undo. Notification/finalization errors can also propagate; do not infer rollback from an exception. No queue clearing, automatic retry or global Undo belongs in a caller’s error handler.
title: Perpendicular Guides uses the same warning

text: The background tools remove entire background layer objects, including their stored payload. They do not merely erase contours. Use Clear All Layer Backgrounds or Clear Master Backgrounds for a panel with a preview and an explicit Apply action. The programmatic equivalent below also separates inspection from the write. masters=False includes mapped backgrounds of all foreground layers in the current font, including auxiliary layers. masters=True restricts the plan to master foreground layers. Neither scope means selected glyphs only. A background shared by a master and an excluded auxiliary layer is refused in master-only mode; silently deleting it would change the excluded layer too. Defining these functions makes no edit. Call preview_backgrounds() in FontLab, inspect the printed glyph/background names, then explicitly pass its returned value to clear_previewed_backgrounds() . Pass masters=True to preview the master-only scope. A preview is bound to its original font and scope: the writer rechecks it before history and refuses stale facts rather than silently rescanning and applying a different plan. from fontlabapp.masters.background.clear.model import plan as background_plan from fontlabapp.masters.background.clear.native import Backend as BackgroundBackend from fontlabapp.core.edit_guards import append_note def preview_backgrounds ( * , masters = False ): backend = BackgroundBackend () source = backend . capture () if source is None : raise ValueError ( "Open a font before previewing backgrounds." ) for removal in background_plan ( source , masters ): print ( f " { removal . glyph } : { removal . mask_name } " ) return backend , source , masters def clear_previewed_backgrounds ( preview ): backend , source , masters = preview disclosure = { "pending_updates" : (), "pending_note" : "" } try : result = backend . apply ( source , masters , disclosure = disclosure ) except BaseException as error : # Report the action's warning, then propagate interruptions unchanged. print ( append_note ( f "Background clearing failed: { error } " , disclosure )) raise print ( append_note ( f "Removed { result [ 'backgrounds' ] } backgrounds from " f " { result [ 'layers' ] } foreground layers in { result [ 'glyphs' ] } glyphs." , result , )) return result backgrounds counts confirmed object removals; layers counts the affected foreground layers, which can differ when backgrounds are shared. glyphs counts owner glyphs. A no-op returns zero counts and empty disclosure without sampling the native queue. A nonempty warning is reported once by this wrapper; the supplied dictionary prevents the backend from printing it separately. Active or locked backgrounds, invalid ownership/mapping, affected automatic layers or automatic dependants, and unsupported history scope can still cause refusal. Queue disclosure does not waive these guards. A refused domain remains an incomplete compatibility boundary, not proof of equivalent original behavior. A failure after an attempted removal may leave changes in the font. Ordinary partial-write errors report attempted and confirmed removal counts and direct the user to Undo. Interruptions stop further removals, attempt remaining date updates and notification, then propagate the original interruption with recovery notes. The wrapper preserves those notes by re-raising the same exception. Neither cleanup nor an exception proves rollback, successful Undo, or that native cleanup finished within a deadline. Do not automatically retry the operation.
title: Preview complete background removal

text: The Raise Ascender formatter and caller are checked against the ordinary App artifact. Formatting uses the actual shared helper; wrapper success/no-op/failure tests substitute the native backend. Those tests prove message composition, disclosure forwarding and exception propagation. They do not prove FontLab editing, native window behavior, whole-font preservation or successful Undo/Redo. The writer’s artifact tests and its dedicated native qualification are separate requirements. The background example is also executed verbatim against the installed App backend and planner. Owned native doubles cover master/auxiliary scope, stale previews, no-op, partial removal and interruption. The backend itself is not replaced. These checks still do not exercise FontLab's compiled object model, native history, saved files, rendered documentation or publication.
title: Verification boundary
Choose the original node-duplication scope explicitly

text: Scriptmix now exposes three distinct Node Duplicator actions. They use App's guarded node_duplicator_native.duplicate_selected_nodes entry point, introduced in the matching 0.2.26.dev333 artifact. Older rescued adapters lack that name. Keep the separate Node Duplicator panel for its per-glyph reference selection, preview and declared-master controls. Menu action in Contours Source policy Duplicate Nodes All Foreground Layers Broadcast the first selected layer's on-curve indices to every stored foreground layer of each selected parent occurrence. Duplicate Nodes Current Layer Copy selected on-curves in the first selected layer only. Duplicate Nodes with Two Handles First selected layer only; insert two coincident controls and a copied curve endpoint per selected on-curve. The two-handle source's filename says “all masters”, but its body has no all-master loop. The actions preserve that distinction. All-layer mode retains auxiliary-layer identities and repeated parents; two layers with the same name remain separate targets. Missing target path/node indices are reported. These are immediate actions. Select nodes, activate the appropriate Font or Glyph window, and run the chosen menu entry. A broadcast that includes owners outside the active Glyph canvas is refused before staging; activate the Font window for that edit. Queued glyph ids are disclosed without clearing them. Automatic dependants, shared owners, hinted topology and unsupported generated or control mappings have explicit refusals. The following experiments execute the actual immutable App planning engine. They use invented node/layer identities and metadata, with no FontLab, Qt, framework, font, preference or document access. They do not establish native selection projection, copy fidelity, history or saved-font acceptance.
title: Choose the original node-duplication scope explicitly

text: Execute this setup afresh before each tagged experiment. Layers10/11 share one parent;20/21 share another. The occurrence list selects the first parent twice. Only node1 in the first selected layer supplies the reference selection. The native adapter keeps display names separately from these stable identities. from dataclasses import replace from fontlabapp.node_duplicator import Node , Path , Layer , Source , plan def owned_source (): def node ( key ): return Node ( key , key + 0.125 , key + 0.375 , "line" , 8 , f "node- { key } " , (( "corner_smooth" , 0.375 ),)) layers = tuple ( Layer ( key , glyph , ( Path ( key * 10 , ( node ( a ), node ( a + 1 )), False ),)) for key , glyph , a in [( 10 , 1 , 1 ), ( 11 , 1 , 3 ), ( 20 , 2 , 5 ), ( 21 , 2 , 7 )] ) return Source ( layers , ( 10 , 11 , 20 ), (( 0 , 1 ),), True )
title: Prepare an owned source graph

text: Both foreground layers of the first parent receive two insertions. Both layers of the second receive one, even though they have no independent selected node. The source graph remains unchanged. History enrollment can deduplicate owners; the operation program must retain repeated occurrences. source = owned_source () result = plan ( source , "all" ) assert result . inserted == 6 assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in result . layers ] == [ 4 , 4 , 3 , 3 ] assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in source . layers ] == [ 2 , 2 , 2 , 2 ] assert [ operation . layer for operation in result . operations ] == [ 10 , 11 , 10 , 11 , 20 , 21 ] assert result . skipped == ()
title: Replay each selected parent occurrence

text: Current mode inserts one line copy. Handles mode inserts two fresh controls and a curve endpoint copied from the target. The copied endpoint keeps its name, coordinates and properties; the new controls do not pretend to be copies. Only the first selected layer changes in either mode. source = owned_source () current , handles = plan ( source , "current" ), plan ( source , "handles" ) assert current . inserted == 1 and handles . inserted == 3 assert [ len ( layer . paths [ 0 ] . nodes ) for layer in current . layers ] == [ 3 , 2 , 2 , 2 ] nodes = handles . layers [ 0 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes assert [ node . kind for node in nodes ] == [ "line" , "off" , "off" , "curve" , "line" ] original , copied = source . layers [ 0 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes [ 0 ], nodes [ 3 ] assert ( copied . x , copied . y , copied . name , copied . properties ) == ( original . x , original . y , original . name , original . properties ) assert nodes [ 1 ] . name == nodes [ 2 ] . name == "" assert nodes [ 1 ] . properties == nodes [ 2 ] . properties == () assert handles . layers [ 1 :] == source . layers [ 1 :]
title: Keep current-layer and handle semantics distinct

text: The original all-layer policy uses fixed reference indices. It does not require every target to have identical topology. Here one target has no path and another has too few nodes. Both skips retain their target identities and exact indices; the native result window supplies captured glyph/layer names alongside them. source = owned_source () layers = list ( source . layers ) layers [ 2 ] = replace ( layers [ 2 ], paths = ()) short = replace ( layers [ 3 ] . paths [ 0 ], nodes = layers [ 3 ] . paths [ 0 ] . nodes [: 1 ]) layers [ 3 ] = replace ( layers [ 3 ], paths = ( short ,)) source = replace ( source , layers = tuple ( layers ), selection = (( 0 , 2 ),)) result = plan ( source , "all" ) assert result . inserted == 4 assert result . skipped == (( 2 , 20 , 0 , 1 ), ( 2 , 21 , 0 , 1 ))
title: Report unavailable target indices

text: A visual selection can contain objects other than editable on-curves. All mode asks for nodes when none are selected. Current mode uses the original truth of the entire selection; handle mode has no corresponding message branch. All three produce no insertions in this owned example. source = replace ( owned_source (), selection = (), any_selection = True ) all_layers = plan ( source , "all" ) current = plan ( source , "current" ) handles = plan ( source , "handles" ) assert all_layers . inserted == current . inserted == handles . inserted == 0 assert all_layers . no_selection_message is True assert current . no_selection_message is False assert handles . no_selection_message is False
title: Preserve the original empty-selection message rules

text: The native boundary captures and rechecks context before history, stages detached copies and uses current history-scope guards. It checks copied metadata and exact old-node state, and reports failed writes. Cleanup removes only exact owned new identities while its deadline permits; it stops further mutations after expiry. WriteError.pending_nodes retains owned contour/node handles for inspection. history_finalized records whether the notification returned successfully; it does not prove actual Undo/Redo or complete restoration. Inspect the affected font and history before retrying. Do not clear native update queues, normalize unrelated dates or discard a failed receipt to obtain a green result. The result window uses the shared parent/priority/lifecycle helper. Owned Qt tests cover parenting, the topmost flag, Close and reopen. Actual macOS FontLab stacking and lifetime, four-font full preservation, Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen, compiled binding behavior and release/promotion remain separate requirements. These behavior-only rewrites credit Fernando Díaz and Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts , whose retained README declares Apache-2.0. Original source identities stay separate in Scriptmix's provenance/backlog; no original body is redistributed here.
title: Handle a partial failure without a blind retry
Keep tool windows usable and recoverable

text: Keep the returned owner until its window has closed successfully. A failed Close must leave a reachable window and its exact signal records available for retry. This guide describes the dialog-ownership App candidate; it is not a released minimum version or evidence of native FontLab stacking.
title: Keep tool windows usable and recoverable

text: Use FontLab's existing application and PythonQt. This example belongs inside FontLab; do not install PySide6 there or start another application event loop. from fly import fl , qt import fly.ap.widgets as widgets def build ( content ): layout = qt . QtGui . QVBoxLayout ( content ) layout . addWidget ( qt . QtGui . QLabel ( "Inspect the current font here." , content )) owned_panel = widgets . create_panel ( fl . MainWindow (), "Inspection" , build , "right" ) # Keep owned_panel. When finished, retain it if close returns False or raises. accepted = owned_panel . close () The Unicode Issues Dock uses this same factory. A hidden MainWindow produces a floating dock. Later undocking also requests the TypeRig-style priority hint; the dock keeps its parent, area, content and native window type. Common Glyphs applies priority inside its existing bounded display/recovery path. Plugin panels and filter dialogs request priority through OwnedMenus.tool_window ; their shell is disposable, while the supplied plugin content remains caller-owned. The generic script launcher retains an exact candidate when flags, show or raise fails. A later launch closes that candidate before constructing its replacement. It also preserves an old owner whose Close refuses or raises. Some panels have a stronger, dedicated failed-owner fence; preserve that panel's recovery protocol.
title: Open a dock inside FontLab

text: The following setup is for a separate Python 3.11 process with App's test extra. It uses actual Qt widgets and the actual App helpers over an injected binding namespace. It never contacts FontLab, reads a font or proves macOS host stacking. Run the setup afresh for each experiment; retain the QApplication for the process. import os import sys assert not { "fontlab" , "FL" , "PythonQt" } . intersection ( sys . modules ) os . environ . setdefault ( "QT_QPA_PLATFORM" , "offscreen" ) from contextlib import contextmanager from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest.mock import patch from PySide6 import QtCore , QtWidgets from shiboken6 import isValid import fontlabapp.widgets as widgets APP = QtWidgets . QApplication . instance () or QtWidgets . QApplication ([]) BINDING = SimpleNamespace ( QtGui = QtWidgets , QtCore = QtCore ) def drain (): APP . processEvents () QtCore . QCoreApplication . sendPostedEvents ( None , QtCore . QEvent . DeferredDelete ) APP . processEvents () @contextmanager def sandbox ( binding = BINDING , parent_type = QtWidgets . QMainWindow ): parent = parent_type () try : with patch . object ( widgets , "_native" , lambda name : binding ): yield parent finally : if isValid ( parent ): parent . deleteLater () drain ()
title: Run these standalone experiments separately

text: with sandbox () as parent : owned = widgets . create_panel ( parent , "Report" , None , "right" ) dock , content = owned . widget , owned . content assert dock . parentWidget () is parent and dock . widget () is content assert dock . isFloating () and dock . isVisible () assert dock . windowFlags () & QtCore . Qt . WindowStaysOnTopHint assert parent . dockWidgetArea ( dock ) == QtCore . Qt . RightDockWidgetArea assert owned . close () is True drain () assert owned . closed and not isValid ( dock )
title: A hidden host still exposes an owned dock

text: with sandbox () as parent : parent . show () owned = widgets . create_panel ( parent , "Report" , None , "left" ) dock = owned . widget assert not dock . isFloating () dock . setFloating ( True ) assert dock . isFloating () and dock . isVisible () assert dock . windowFlags () & QtCore . Qt . WindowStaysOnTopHint dock . setFloating ( False ) assert not dock . isFloating () and dock . widget () is owned . content assert owned . close ()
title: Docking stays available when the host is visible

text: class Draft ( QtWidgets . QDialog ): allow_close = False def closeEvent ( self , event ): event . accept () if self . allow_close else event . ignore () with sandbox () as parent : dialog = Draft ( parent ) owned = widgets . OwnedWidget ( dialog , dialog ) dialog . show () assert owned . close () is False assert not owned . closed and owned . widget is dialog and dialog . isVisible () dialog . allow_close = True assert owned . close () is True drain () assert owned . closed and not isValid ( dialog )
title: A refused Close keeps its visible owner

text: class Host ( QtWidgets . QMainWindow ): fail_removal = True def removeDockWidget ( self , dock ): if self . fail_removal : raise RuntimeError ( "owned removal failed" ) QtWidgets . QMainWindow . removeDockWidget ( self , dock ) with sandbox ( parent_type = Host ) as parent : owned = widgets . create_panel ( parent , "Report" , None , "right" ) dock = owned . widget try : owned . close () except RuntimeError as error : assert str ( error ) == "owned removal failed" else : raise AssertionError ( "The removal failure was hidden" ) assert owned . widget is dock and not owned . closed and isValid ( dock ) parent . fail_removal = False assert owned . close () drain () assert not isValid ( dock )
title: Unregistration failure retains the unfinished stage

text: class Refusing ( QtWidgets . QDialog ): allow_close = False def closeEvent ( self , event ): event . accept () if self . allow_close else event . ignore () binding = SimpleNamespace ( QtGui = SimpleNamespace ( QDialog = Refusing ), QtCore = QtCore ) with sandbox ( binding ) as parent : original = ValueError ( "report setup failed" ) def fail ( content ): raise original try : widgets . create_dialog ( parent , "Report" , fail ) except ExceptionGroup as failure : assert failure . exceptions [ 0 ] is original recovery = failure . owner assert not recovery . closed and isinstance ( recovery . widget , Refusing ) recovery . widget . allow_close = True assert recovery . close () else : raise AssertionError ( "Refused cleanup lost its recovery owner" )
