text: A glyph's stored Unicode is editable font data. A name-based Glyph Info lookup asks for database metadata. These differ when a glyph has been re-encoded: a script that resets Unicode cannot use the current encoding as its reference. Omitting font or passing font=None queries the shared manager without reading the active font. An explicit font selects font.glyphsInfo() ; the earlier unconditional .localData refusal is superseded. Integer Name dispatch differs by complete Glyphs2/3/4 profile. The manager/profile guide provides current document selection, exact keywords, formatting, forwarding and provider examples. Its default Glyphs4 Unicode keyword is string_or_int ; Glyphs2/3 retain String with their separate integer contracts. This diagnostic fixture runs outside FontLab. It instantiates the application facade with owned model/bridge doubles; it does not activate GlyphsApp, load a native host or edit an open font. The deliberately incorrect encoding on A remains untouched after the query. from types import SimpleNamespace from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp.application import GSApplication current_glyph = SimpleNamespace ( name = "A" , unicode = "0042" , category = "Symbol" , subCategory = None , script = "custom-script" , case = 2 , layers = [], ) local = owned_parsed_manager () current_font = SimpleNamespace ( glyphs = { "A" : current_glyph }, glyphsInfo = lambda : local ) model = SimpleNamespace ( font = current_font ) # This fixture never calls bridge methods or reads/writes persistent defaults. app = GSApplication ( model , object (), {}, None , lambda * args : None ) info = app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" ) assert info . unicode == "0041" , "Name-derived data must not copy current encoding" assert info . category == "Letter" assert info . script == "latin" assert current_glyph . script == "custom-script" , "A lookup must not edit script metadata" # Filter by database script metadata; an unassigned script remains None. names = [ "A" , "Alpha" , "alpha" , "acutecomb" ] greek = [ name for name in names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . script == "greek" ] assert greek == [ "Alpha" , "alpha" ] assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "acutecomb" ) . script is None # Case is a database enum: upper=1, lower=2, not a Unicode category. case_names = [ "A" , "a" , "exclam" , "less" , "acutecomb" ] upper = [ name for name in case_names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . case == 1 ] lower = [ name for name in case_names if app . glyphInfoForName ( name ) . case == 2 ] assert upper == [ "A" , "exclam" ] assert lower == [ "a" , "less" , "acutecomb" ] assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "acutecomb" ) . category == "Mark" assert current_glyph . case == 2 , "A lookup must not edit case metadata" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = None ) . unicode == "0041" assert current_glyph . unicode == "0042" , "A lookup must not edit the glyph" assert app . glyphInfoForName ( "A" , font = current_font ) is local . glyphInfoForName_ ( "A" ) assert current_glyph . unicode == "0042" , "Explicit lookup must not edit current encoding" The read-only script field snapshots metadata supplied by the database. This example uses it to select Greek names without changing the font. An unassigned script stays None ; do not treat that as a missing glyph or invent a script from its Unicode. The read-only case field also snapshots database metadata. Its values are no-case (0), upper (1), lower (2), small-caps (3), minor (4) and other (5). They are not Unicode general categories: exclam has upper case metadata, while less and the combining mark acutecomb have lower case metadata. Missing case metadata maps to no-case; an unknown label raises an unsupported capability error. Other Glyph Info fields remain incomplete. This fixture needs the private global-lookup, script-field and case-field repairs. Several uncommitted builds share 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548.d20261101 ; version text alone does not identify them. title: Query glyph metadata without copying the current encoding

text: GSGlyph.case is mutable glyph metadata; GSGlyphInfo.case above is a read-only database snapshot. A glyph can have a temporary case value while storeCase is false. Setting that flag to true preserves the current value through supported name changes and metadata refreshes. Setting an attached glyph's flag from true to false restores its database default. Assigning false when it is already false leaves a temporary value intact. The following owned fixture runs outside FontLab. It demonstrates the same minor-figure predicate used by kerning scripts, then changes case without editing an open font. FakeBackend supplies the attachment target; it is not a font file. from fontlab_glyport.errors import UnsupportedCapability from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend names = [ "A" , "ordfeminine" , "one" ] assert [ name for name in names if GSGlyph ( name ) . case == 4 ] == [ "ordfeminine" ] glyph = GSGlyph ( "f_f_i" ) assert glyph . case == 2 glyph . case = 3 assert glyph . storeCase is False glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 3 # An unchanged flag does not refresh metadata. font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) assert glyph . case == 3 # Unique attachment retains the temporary value. glyph . storeCase = True glyph . name = "less" assert glyph . case == 3 # The stored value survives this name change. glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 2 # Attached reset restores the database classification. copied = glyph . copy () copied . storeCase = True copied . case = 5 assert glyph . case == 2 try : copied . storeCase = False except UnsupportedCapability as error : assert error . capability == "GSGlyph.storeCase.detachedReset" else : raise AssertionError ( "Detached reset is not yet qualified" ) assert ( copied . case , copied . storeCase ) == ( 5 , True ) Detached true-to-false reset currently refuses before mutation; its upstream manager behavior still needs qualification. Custom global/font-local databases, synthesized names and complete updateGlyphInfo behavior remain incomplete. That historical candidate refused unknown-name updates. This fixture does not prove native history, saved/reopened metadata or complete kerning-script workflows. The lifecycle candidate uses the same private development version as the earlier case-field build above. text: GSGlyph.script reads named-glyph metadata, including for unencoded glyphs. Assignment changes the current value without enabling storeScript . An enabled flag preserves the value through supported name changes and refreshes. Disabling it on an attached glyph restores the database default. An already-false flag leaves a temporary assignment intact. None and an empty string are distinct explicit values. This owned fixture runs outside FontLab. It exercises the draft-before-append pattern used by script builders, followed by a stored override and reset. from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = GSGlyph ( "f_f" ) assert glyph . script == "latin" glyph . script = "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "Rovas" font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) assert glyph . script == "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = True glyph . name = "Alpha" assert glyph . script == "Rovas" glyph . storeScript = False assert glyph . script == "greek" glyph . script = None assert glyph . script is None # Explicit None does not fall back to Greek. copied = glyph . copy () assert copied . script is None copied . script = "" assert copied . script == "" and glyph . script is None with font . glyphsInfo () . _scope (): copied . name = "A-cy" assert copied . script == "cyrillic" # A known name refreshes unstored metadata. Detached true-to-false reset refuses before mutation, as with case metadata. Custom metadata managers, synthesized names, complete original-script workflows, native Undo/Redo and saved/reopened metadata remain unqualified. The fixture uses an owned backend double and does not edit any font file. The script-lifecycle candidate retains version 1.0.8.dev58+g753b55548.d20261101 . title: Preserve a glyph's script override

text: The source candidate now supports independent category , subCategory , storeCategory and storeSubCategory values. Classification accepts strings, including the empty string, or None . Assigning Unicode alone does not refresh classification. Turning an enabled storage flag off refreshes only that field; a flag already off is a no-op. Detached resets remain explicitly unsupported. Case, script and classification resets share Unicode-first resolution. For an A encoded as 0061 , case resets to lowercase; for 0A15 , script resets to Gurmukhi. The first resolvable encoding wins, including synthesized metadata: an unassigned 0378 prevents a later 0A15 from supplying Gurmukhi metadata, while 10FFFF , which yields no record, allows the next encoding to be tried. The Icon and SF-Symbol categories use the audited keep-name path. This owned example exercises the shared resolver without opening FontLab: from fontlab_glyport.model import Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font glyph = font . glyphs [ "A" ] glyph . unicodes = [ "0061" ] glyph . category = "Symbol" glyph . storeCategory = True glyph . case = 3 glyph . storeCase = True glyph . storeCase = False assert glyph . case == 2 # Unicode metadata wins over the name A. assert glyph . category == "Symbol" and glyph . storeCategory glyph . storeCategory = False assert glyph . category == "Letter" assert glyph . name == "A" and glyph . unicodes == [ "0061" ] These are owned offline checks against retained upstream analysis, not native measurements. Custom data, full ROS mapping, complex small-cap mapping and language suffixes remain unqualified. The current private parameter/presentation update is described in the ordered parameter guide . Additional encodings now follow the audited helper gates; native workflow acceptance remains open. title: Classification and shared resolver

text: Refreshing an attached uppercase glyph can add its lowercase encoding when no other glyph owns that code. I can also gain dotless i; each ownership check is independent. Refresh applies the resolved metadata’s encoding list plus these additions; it does not preserve every arbitrary previous glyph encoding. Additions preserve the resolved list’s order and do not duplicate its entries. This uses the glyph's current case/script, including temporary overrides, before stored metadata overlays. Resetting a storage flag does not write encodings. The owned example below runs without FontLab: from fontlab_glyport.model import GSGlyph , Model from fontlab_glyport.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () glyph = GSGlyph ( "I" ) font . glyphs . append ( glyph ) glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0069" , "0131" ] glyph . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert glyph . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0069" , "0131" ] # No duplicates. other_font = Model ( FakeBackend ()) . font other_font . parent . _local_glyph_info = owned_parsed_manager () other_font . glyphs . append ( GSGlyph ( "i" )) capital = GSGlyph ( "I" ) other_font . glyphs . append ( capital ) capital . updateGlyphInfo ( changeName = False ) assert capital . unicodes == [ "0049" , "0131" ] # Another glyph owns ordinary i. Greek-script expansion requires both Phi and Sigma encodings in the font. U+0130 and the audited out-of-range sentinel bypass expansion. Ordinary rename and explicit refresh remain distinct: rename clears non-PUA encodings before resolution, while a subsequent refresh can add encodings. Parentless glyphs and keep-name categories have separate audited branches. The retained parentless Arabic branch can yield no metadata; it is not equivalent to attached refresh. Legacy-only Arabic .isol data does not become primary Unicode automatically. The bundled Unicode17 scalar mapping matches actual NSString.lowercaseString for all1,112,064 valid scalars on macOS27.2. Python3.11 casing differs on55scalars. This pins that measured casing contract, not all Foundation versions. The public data and licence ship with the package; no Objective-C bridge is loaded for this operation. Native history/reopen, complete local initialization and full ROS mapping remain unqualified. The newer source/artifact-tested Arabic presentation stage is described in the ordered parameter guide ; it does not establish native font-workflow acceptance.

title: What is supported

text: Compatibility is partial and still being extended; each run records a receipt with the outcome, and unsupported features raise UnsupportedCapability at the script line instead of failing silently. Native tools have no toolbar icon, never claim keys (so FontLab shortcuts keep working, with no shortcut override), and paint only while active. FontLab always reports the active tool as select. Bundles that ship only compiled macOS code cannot run. Creating glyphs makes FontLab rebuild auto-layer composites. Glyport restores existing composites afterwards and refuses with a named reason when it cannot. A FontLab defect can still drop component locks and attaching anchors on composites it rebuilds. Edits on auto layers (outlines, anchors, guides, hints, width, background) are refused before anything changes: telling FontLab about an auto-layer edit makes it rebuild every auto layer in the font. Test with a copy of your font: scripts can change the font they run on. See the Glyphs compatibility guide . Reference: fontlab_glyport .
title: Limits

text: Native triage on FontLab 9.0.9802 ran 98 corpus Glyphs plugins and scripts through Glyport on an owned font (final code). Pass means the target loaded, registered its menu, tool or window, ran the hooks the harness could trigger without errors, and closed cleanly. Partial means it loaded and ran but a hook raised. Fail means it did not load or did not close. Kind Targets Pass Partial Fail Reporters 30 14 9 7 Tools 7 2 2 3 Filters 12 11 0 1 Palettes 7 5 0 2 General plugins 12 4 0 8 Scripts 30 19 1 10 Total 98 55 12 31 A pass does not prove a plugin's whole behaviour: buttons, dialogs, filter output and outline edits were not exercised, and filters were only installed. Main known gaps: Compiled Objective-C bundles (for example ShowAngledHandles) have no Python entry point and cannot run. The triage environment lacked glyphsLib , which Glyport declares as a dependency. Plugins that import it failed there; a complete install avoids that failure class, so the counts understate what a complete install passes. Some AppKit and Cocoa members are missing (for example NSGradient , NSBeep and a few layout and window constants), and a few Glyphs model members are absent.

text: Grablab captures FontLab's interface for documentation and tests: panels, menus, Glyph and Font windows, screens and widgets, as PNG, SVG or PDF with title and description metadata.
title: grablab

text: Install fontlab-grablab together with fontlab-fontlabapp into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Importing grablab is host-free; capturing needs FontLab.
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from grablab import Grab capture = Grab ( grab_canvas = False , grab_screens = False ) capture . newGrab () paths = capture . grabPanel ( "elements" ) print ( paths )
title: Quick start

text: Capture a widget, including a Fontlabapp drawing overlay, as SVG and PNG: from pathlib import Path from fontlabapp import Application from grablab import Grab app = Application () folder = Path . home () / "Desktop" / "captures" folder . mkdir ( exist_ok = True ) grab = Grab ( application = app , folder_base = folder ) with app . control as fl : grab . getWidgetSVG ( fl . preview . widget , folder / "preview.svg" )

text: Instamix installs Python distributions, source projects and ready extensions into FontLab's user data folder. Its bootstrap uses only Python's standard library; small selection and message helpers import FontLab's PythonQt lazily. It does not provide another application window or a second Qt runtime.
title: Instamix

text: Download the standalone install.vfpy and open it in FontLab. Use 1.0.9 or newer before upgrading legacy installations: 1.0.8 could remove other legacy-owned files when replacement failed. Current generated project stubs check for the corrected rollback capability before deployment; they replace an older provider through the validated wheel bootstrap or stop if replacement fails. See Install and connect .
title: Start with the standalone installer

text: These root functions are lazy exports. Importing Instamix does not import native FontLab modules: from pathlib import Path import fontlab_instamix as im im . install_packages ( "fonttools>=4" ) records = im . install ( Path ( "tools.fontlabextz" )) print ( im . installed ()) kept_paths = im . uninstall ( "com.example.tools" ) install_packages(*specs, data=None) accepts distribution requirements, including git+ URLs. It refreshes import caches; it does not infer a distribution from an import name or reload an imported binary module. install(path, data=None) accepts an extension folder, its root manifest.fontlabextj , or an archive. installed(data=None) returns installation records; uninstall(id, data=None) returns paths kept because the deployed files changed. install_project(start, data=None) reads the nearest pyproject.toml at or above a source path. Its [tool.fontlab-install] table names packages, Scripts, bundles and requirements. Generate its shared entry point with: uvx --from "fontlab-python-instamix>=1.0.9" fontlab-instamix stub path/to/project The command refuses an existing install.vfpy unless --force is explicit. data_dir(explicit=None) resolves the data folder; the explicit argument wins, then FONTLAB_DATA_DIR , native dataPathDefault , and the platform default. When the app's custom dataPath differs, pass that chosen path explicitly.
title: Python entry points

text: Inside FontLab, target discovery uses the embedded Python major/minor version and process architecture. Outside it, defaults mean FontLab 9's Python 3.11 on the current OS and architecture, not a remotely discovered host. python_version() reports the actual running Python; it is not the standalone installation default. Target helpers belong to the env submodule, not the root lazy exports: from pathlib import Path from fontlab_instamix import env , packages chosen = env . Target ( "3.11" , "darwin" , "arm64" ) data = env . data_dir ( Path ( "scratch/FontLab 9" )) print ( env . site_packages ( data , version = chosen . version )) # Explicit provider operation; this does not contact a running FontLab: packages . install ( data , [ "fonttools>=4" ], target = chosen ) Use "win32" and "x86_64" for a Windows x64 target. uv selects a matching standalone interpreter, kept separate from FontLab's executable. The verified <data>/.venv reads the canonical <data>/python/<version>/site-packages directory through its own managed .pth ; packages install into that canonical directory. uv is kept under <data>/python/uv . An incompatible venv or unrelated managed-path file is refused without replacement. The external CLI has env , pkg , ext , bootstrap , wrap , pack , stub , uv and venv commands. Put global options before the subcommand: fontlab-instamix --data-dir "scratch/FontLab 9" env fontlab-instamix --data-dir "scratch/FontLab 9" pkg install fonttools Optional Remopy enables --remote , where the host supplies target facts and a shared-filesystem nonce proves access. uv work runs externally. A timeout is not host cancellation; no automatic replay is safe. The 9.1.9813 bridge defect and its direct-script alternative are described in Install and connect .
title: Targets and the shared environment

text: A canonical com.example.tools.fontlabext folder contains a root manifest: { "id" : "com.example.tools" , "name" : "Example Tools" , "version" : "1.0.0" , "python" : { "requires" : [ "fonttools>=4" ]}, "install" : [{ "from" : "scripts" , "to" : "Scripts/{}" }] } Its scripts directory supplies the payload. The manifest id must match the folder name without .fontlabext . A .fontlabextz ZIP contains one or more whole extension folders, not just their contents; the download's basename has no identity meaning. Extensions are retained under Extensions/Library , then linked or copied into normal deployment locations. Production scripts use those normal locations, not Library paths. Targets include Scripts , Actions , Codepage , Encoding , Data and site-packages . Scripts/. means that target's root; {} expands to the extension id, and {name} reads vars.name . Absolute paths, parent escapes, unknown targets/variables and ambiguous archive identities are refused. Optional archive installer hooks require explicit run_hooks=True ; remote hook execution is refused. Install records still track each extension separately. Wrap a single script without executing it, or pack several complete extensions: fontlab-instamix wrap width_report.py --out dist --id com.example.width-report --name "Width Report" --version 1 .0.0 --zip fontlab-instamix pack com.example.first.fontlabext com.example.second.fontlabext --out tools.fontlabextz For draft plugins, add explicit --kind , --plugin-id , --name , --entry and --min-app-version . Canonical suffixes are .fontlabreporter , .fontlabfilter , .fontlabtool , .fontlabpalette and .fontlabgeneral ; use App 1.2.31 or newer. Wrapping validates metadata without importing the draft or proving native behavior. Inside a script, from fontlab_instamix.gui import install_selected followed by install_selected() selects multiple archives/manifests. folder=True selects one extension directory. These are optional PythonQt helpers, not a standalone GUI.
title: Extension folders and archives

text: Current project upgrades restore affected legacy-owned files, links, modes and receipts if replacement fails. An owner-edited or unowned conflict is a reason to stop and inspect the named path, not to delete it. If restoration fails, the exception names a retained recovery folder; keep that folder and its mapping. The transaction covers the project's deployed files and ownership records; separately installed dependencies and completed independent installs can remain. An error can carry installed_records for work completed before a later failure. A multi-extension archive must not be treated as all-or-nothing without checking that result. Uninstall preserves changed deployed files and leaves separately installed shared Python dependencies. Keep filesystem/native tests, ordinary wheel installation and actual FontLab/Windows acceptance separate.
title: Upgrades, removal and failures

text: fontlab_instamix lists the public API.
title: Reference

text: Pens implements the fontTools Pen and PointPen protocol for FontLab 9 with no runtime dependencies. For the selected APIs it keeps the class and function names of fontTools.pens , so protocol-compatible code draws, measures, transforms and reverses outlines without installing fontTools. It is not the complete fontTools pen set. Fontport builds its FontGate point pens on it.
title: Pens

text: Pens is not on a package index. Install a tagged release from GitHub, or open install.vfpy from a checkout in FontLab and restart; see Install into FontLab . It needs Python 3.11 or later. Importing fontlab_pens is safe outside FontLab: the native pens load fontgate and fontlab lazily.
title: Install

text: from fontlab_pens import BoundsPen , RecordingPen , TransformPen rec = RecordingPen () pen = TransformPen ( rec , ( 2 , 0 , 0 , 2 , 10 , 0 )) pen . moveTo (( 0 , 0 )) pen . curveTo (( 0 , 50 ), ( 50 , 100 ), ( 100 , 100 )) pen . closePath () print ( rec . value )
title: Quick start

text: Native pens must target an explicit layer or element, never a glyph. Only the selected fontTools pen APIs are implemented; see the API reference. See the Pens API reference .
title: Limits

text: Plugmix is a package of native FontLab 9 plugins. It has five plugin kinds: reporters (toggleable, read-only overlays on the Glyph window), filters (undoable edits to selected glyphs), palettes (dockable panels), tools (native FontLab tools) and General plugins (menu commands and font events). Plugmix uses FontLab's PythonQt and, on older builds, Fontlabapp's editor painters. It does not use PySide2, and it does not emulate Glyphs.app. Under revision Plugmix is being revised. This page describes the stable concepts. Exact module names and defaults can still change. Bundle delivery and the compatibility runtime The current extension pack uses App's bundle loader. New bundles use lowercase .fontlabreporter , .fontlabfilter , .fontlabtool , .fontlabpalette and .fontlabgeneral suffixes and require App 1.2.31 or newer. Instamix installs their extension payloads and refuses conflicting modified/unowned legacy bundles. Use Instamix 1.0.9 or newer for source-project upgrades. The separate fontlab_plugmix compatibility runtime described below remains supported; do not activate both representations of the same plugins in one session. See Instamix and the current release inputs .
title: Plugmix

text: FontLab 9 builds with native canvas painters expose two Python hooks on the host itself: a canvas painter ( flCanvas.appendPythonPainter ) and a workspace tool ( flWorkspace.registerPythonTool ). See Native Python hooks in FontLab 9 . Plugmix reporters build on the painter hook. Registry. Finds plugins of every kind, remembers your choices, and attaches or detaches them. Built-in plugins and plugins published through the fontlab_plugmix.plugins entry-point group are discovered the same way, and the kind comes from the class's base class. A plugin needs a unique name and a human-readable title ; names are unique across kinds. Native-painter backend. When flCanvas.appendPythonPainter exists, Plugmix attaches one painter per Glyph window as it becomes active and registers each reporter on it. Reporters with layer = "background" paint under the glyph; the others paint over it. On older builds the backend falls back to Fontlabapp's EditorPainters , paints everything over the canvas and logs the background substitution once. Coordinates. A glyph point is mapped through the glyph's position in its text block, then the text block's placement, then canvas.mapToViewportF into viewport pixels. Cost. Each reporter reads the glyph again on every repaint. That is fine for the built-in set but adds up with many reporters enabled. Plugins compute from immutable, plain-Python snapshots, so you can test them without FontLab.
title: How it works

text: Install fontlab-python-plugmix and its fontlab-fontlabapp dependency into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Start Plugmix once per FontLab session from your own initScript.py : try : from fontlab_plugmix import install ; install () except Exception as error : print ( f "Plugmix startup: { error } " ) The package ships this snippet as initScript-snippet.py . Nothing in the package edits a FontLab installation. Alternatively, run Install Plugmix Menu.py from the Script menu. install() adds menu entries and restores your choices: Kind Where it appears Reporter One checkable Plugmix: Show ... action per reporter in the View menu. Filter Plugmix: Delete Small Paths… in the Glyph menu, opening a non-modal parameter dialog. Palette Plugmix: Step and Repeat Panel in the Window menu, checkable, hidden until shown. Tool Plugmix: Tool Smart Select , which registers a native tool when enabled. General Plugmix: Zoom to Selection in the View menu. Choices live in one JSON file in FontLab's Data folder, with these keys: enabled (reporters), enabled_filters , enabled_palettes , enabled_tools , enabled_general and params (last-used filter values). Older files with only enabled still load, filters, tools and General plugins are enabled by default, and enabled_palettes is written only after you choose a visibility. A selection saved under the former name nodes_outside_paths restores as offcurve_outside_bounds . uninstall() removes the actions, overlays and panels and keeps the saved choices.
title: Install

text: Built-in reporters: Reporter Overlay Duplicate Anchor Rings Rings around anchors less than one font unit apart. Node Indexes Contour index beside every on- and off-curve node. Selected Node Coordinates Coordinates beside selected nodes. Two Point Distance Segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes. Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds ( offcurve_outside_bounds ) Off-curve handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle. It tests bounds, not path containment. Center Lines Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines. Vertical Metrics Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline. Angled Handles Rings on off-curve handles outside horizontal, vertical and italic axes. Crosshair Guides through selected nodes. Tops and Bottoms Rings and y labels at tied highest and lowest on-curve positions. Segment Length Straight and flattened curve lengths for selected segments. Glyph Focus Shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender. Emphasise Selected Handles Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes. Anchor Cloud Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors. RSB Line Advance boundary plus RSB and LSB labels. Unitizer Vertical grid at UPM / 18 increments. Nodes Close to Zones Rings on on-curves near zone edges or metric heights. Imprecise Italic Angle Straight segments close to, but not exactly on, the master slant. Smooth Node Angles Handle-angle mismatch and handle-length ratio at smooth nodes.
title: Reporters

text: from fontlab_plugmix import Mark , Reporter class Origin ( Reporter ): name = "origin" title = "Origin" def compute ( self , snapshot ): return [ Mark ( "ring" , (( 0 , 0 ),), diameter_px = 12 ), Mark ( "text" , (( 6 , 6 ),), text = "origin" , text_px = 11 ), ] compute() returns marks in font units. Mark kinds are ring , line , polyline , polygon (with an RGBA fill ) and text ; stroke width, text size and ring diameter are view pixels, so overlays keep their size while you zoom. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph on builds with native painters. Publish the class so Plugmix finds it. In your package's pyproject.toml : [project.entry-points. "fontlab_plugmix.plugins" ] origin = "my_package.reporters:Origin" Reinstall your package and restart FontLab; the reporter appears in the View menu.
title: Write your own reporter

text: A filter computes a proposed edit for one layer from a frozen snapshot and typed values, and Plugmix applies the result to the selected glyphs as one Undo step. Param(key, label, kind, default, minimum=None, maximum=None, choices=()) declares a dialog field. kind is "float" , "int" , "bool" or "choice" ; values outside the declared domain are rejected. LayerEdit(contours=None, advance=None, anchors=None) holds replacement values; None leaves that part of the layer alone. Filter.compute(snapshot, values) returns a LayerEdit . Filter.validate(values) fills defaults and rejects unknown or invalid parameters. from fontlab_plugmix.filter import Filter , LayerEdit class DropOpenPaths ( Filter ): name = "drop_open_paths" title = "Drop Open Paths" params = () def compute ( self , snapshot , values ): kept = tuple ( c for c in snapshot . contours if c . closed ) return LayerEdit ( contours = kept ) The writer currently supports contour deletion. It skips shared or transformed outlines and automatic layers per glyph and still edits the other selected glyphs. Delete Small Paths ( delete_small_paths , one parameter threshold , default 400 font units squared) deletes a closed contour when its area, measured on the flattened curves, is strictly below the threshold. A contour whose flattened bounding-box area is below the threshold is treated the same way. Open paths always stay, and a contour exactly at the threshold stays.
title: Filters

text: A palette is a dockable panel. Palette.build(ui) creates controls once through PaletteUI , refresh(context) runs when the active glyph, master, revision or node selection changes, and close() releases resources. PaletteUI offers label , number , checkbox and button , so palettes import no Qt. One timer serves all visible palettes and stops when none are visible. Step and Repeat ( step_and_repeat ) duplicates the selected contours of the active glyph. count is the number of additional copies, and each copy is shifted by another ( dx , dy ), so offsets accumulate. Apply is one Undo step. It works on the current master layer only: when the Glyph window shows another layer, Apply refuses with a status message instead of writing to the master.
title: Palettes

text: A tool becomes a native FontLab tool through flWorkspace.registerPythonTool . Tool.activate(ctx) and deactivate() bracket its use; press , move , release , double_click , key_down and key_up each take a ToolEvent and return True when they handled it; marks(glyph) returns overlay marks drawn only while the tool is active. ToolContext offers snapshot() , select(indices, toggle=False) , edit(plan_fn, title) and redraw() . Viewport events are mapped through FontLab's pan and zoom and the glyph's text-block transforms. Smart Select drags a rectangle and selects whole contours touched by any node; Shift toggles those contours. It is selection-only and never changes outline geometry. It omits the source plugin's double-click containment and native move handling.
title: Tools

text: A General plugin is a menu command with optional font events. General.start(ctx) and stop() bracket its life, run() handles the command, and on_font_opened(font_id) and on_font_closed(font_id) report fonts by the stable flPackage.fgId , the id that MCP, Remopy and Fontport use. GeneralContext offers notify , snapshot , edit , timer and zoom_selected . Plugmix owns the extra actions and timers a General plugin creates and removes them on uninstall() . General font watchers share the palettes' 250 ms timer. Zoom to Selection fits the active glyph's selected nodes in the canvas with a margin. It omits the source plugin's delayed viewport adjustment. Shortcut conflicts are reported, not overridden. Shortcut handling and keyboard cursor mapping still need an in-app recheck.
title: General plugins

text: The repository's Scripts/ folder holds two ordinary FontLab menu scripts: Scripts/Plugmix/Install Plugmix Menu.py installs the Plugmix menus, and Scripts/Reports/Duplicate Anchor Rings.py runs one reporter from the Script menu. Copy them into FontLab's Scripts folder to use them.
title: The Scripts folder

text: Reporters are read-only. Filters, palettes and tools edit only through Plugmix's shared outline writer. Painting runs inside FontLab's paint event on the GUI thread. Keep compute() quick. The palette refresh key reads the glyph modification timestamp and node selection; confirm that edits outside Plugmix advance it in your build. Native behaviour needs an in-app check: the test suite uses fake Qt and FontLab objects, and some newer reporters have offline coverage only.
title: Limits

text: Pythonqtside lets code written for PySide2 ( QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets , …) run on FontLab's built-in PythonQt. It routes each PySide2 name to the native class and adapts the differences that matter in practice: keyword arguments, property getters, overloads and protected event handlers. It never loads a second Qt binding or creates a QApplication .
title: pythonqtside

text: Install pythonqtside (it depends on Echopy) into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab .
title: Install

text: # Inside FontLab from pythonqtside import QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets widget = QtWidgets . QWidget () # the original native QWidget layout = QtWidgets . QVBoxLayout ( widget ) layout . addWidget ( QtWidgets . QLabel ( "Hello from PySide2-style code" )) widget . show ()
title: Quick start

text: Port an existing PySide2 tool by changing only its import: # from PySide2 import QtCore, QtWidgets from pythonqtside import QtCore , QtWidgets In FontLab 9, natively, QFileDialog.getOpenFileName and getSaveFileName return a str and getOpenFileNames returns a tuple. The adapter always returns PySide2-style pairs instead: (path, "") for the single-file pickers and (list_of_paths, "") for getOpenFileNames . The chosen filter cannot be read back, so a selectedFilter argument is dropped and reported as "" . options keeps its native position, and a result that is already a pair passes through. The repository's examples/pyside2_dialog.py is an unmodified PySide2 dialog that uses this; run it with pythonqtside.run_app("examples/pyside2_dialog.py") and keep the returned handle. Available namespaces: QtCore , QtGui , QtWidgets , QtNetwork , QtOpenGL , QtSvg , QtUiTools , QtXmlPatterns and the combined Qt .
title: Examples

text: Use FontLab's running application; do not call QApplication.exec() . Names alone do not guarantee identical behaviour: enum conversion, ownership and some overloads differ from PySide2. See the PySide2 guide . Qt 6 / PySide6 is not supported (FontLab 9 uses Qt 5). Reference: pythonqtside .
title: Limits

text: Remopy controls a running FontLab 9 from another Python process through FontLab's native MCP server: run code, read values, open and save fonts and call any FontLab tool. It also launches FontLab and submits scripts on macOS.
title: Remopy

text: Install the fontlab-remopy wheel into your ordinary Python 3.11+ environment (not into FontLab). Enable FontLab's MCP server once: fontlab-remopy launch fontlab-remopy --timeout 15 setup setup submits a macro that sets FontLab's mcp.enabled preference and verifies it. From inside FontLab, call fontlab_remopy.enable_mcp() to do the same preference update directly.
title: Install

text: from fontlab_remopy import FontLab with FontLab () as fl : print ( fl . fonts ()) answer = fl . eval ( "value + 2" , value = 40 ) # 42 done = fl . run ( "print(message); result = {'ok': True}" , message = "Hello" ) print ( done . value , done . stdout )
title: Quick start

text: Write a function locally and run it inside FontLab: with FontLab () as fl : @fl . python def metrics ( name : str ): import fontpr return fontpr . get_glyph_metrics ( glyph_name = name ) print ( metrics ( "A" )) # with an open font containing A Run a script file and call tools from the command line: fontlab-remopy tools fontlab-remopy execute example.flpy fontlab-remopy call list_fonts Use AsyncFontLab with async with and await in asynchronous programs. Call any other FontLab tool by name with fl.tool(name, **arguments) . Remopy checks the argument names against the tool's input schema and raises ValueError for an unknown name before anything is sent. This matters because FontLab's MCP server silently drops unknown arguments: set_kerning_pair(master="Bold") would write to the current master. The kerning tools take master_name : with FontLab () as fl : fl . tool ( "list_kerning_pairs" , master_name = "Bold" ) Only names are checked, not types, and tools missing from the catalogue or with open schemas are not checked. The one-shot call_tool function and the CLI call command apply the same check (one catalogue request per call); pass check_arguments=False to opt out. run_python skips the check.
title: Examples

text: Values travel as JSON; native objects cannot be returned directly. FontLab's fixed five-second script deadline applies. A timeout leaves the outcome unknown, so mutating calls are never retried automatically. Launch and file association are macOS only; MCP works wherever FontLab's bridge executable is available. Reference: fontlab_remopy . Remopy is proprietary (© Fontlab Ltd); only its API documentation is published here.
title: Limits

text: Scriptmix ( fontlab-python-scriptmix ) is a menu collection of practical tools for FontLab 9: metrics, names and anchors editors, component writers, master navigation and layer copying, contour editing, kerning editors, proof texts, reports and drawing panels. The tools inspect, proof and edit fonts through FontLab's native APIs, PythonQt and Fontlabapp helpers. Scriptmix is not an installable Python package. It is a set of scripts you copy into FontLab; its pyproject.toml only configures documentation tools.
title: Scriptmix

text: Install matching fontlab-fly , fontlab-fontlabapp and fontlab-fontport into FontLab's Python folder; see Install into FontLab . Some tools also need fontTools , and Glyphs-specific tools use Glyport. Open FontLab's Scripts folder from the application. Copy the category folders from the repository's Scripts/ folder into it. Keep the layout Scripts/<Category>/<Tool>.py ; FontLab accepts one category level. Open a copy of a font, select the glyphs and master, and choose the tool from the Script menu. Each tool's docstring states its controls, scopes and refusals.
title: Install

text: Metrics, Names, Anchors, Components, Masters, Contours, Features, Font Info, Guides, Kerning, Cleanup, Proof, Reports and Utilities. Each is a folder under Scripts/ .
title: Categories

text: Metrics > Scale Advances scales selected advances by a percentage, with a preview, keeping outlines centred. Masters > Duplicate Current Layer backs up the current master or all masters. Names > Duplicate Unicodes scans the font and lets you choose assignments to keep or remove. Proof > Text Filter simplifies proof text with persistent input and regex fields.
title: Examples

text: Source tests do not establish correct Undo/Redo, saved font state or panel lifetime inside FontLab; native acceptance is tracked separately in the repository. Work on owned copies of fonts. See the repository's README and porting backlog for the full tool list and status. Where a task needs an interface or helper you write yourself, build it on Fontlabapp .
title: Limits

text: TypeRig is Vassil Kateliev's font-development library: outline objects, points and contours, interpolation and adaptive scaling, and proxies over FontLab's objects. This package distributes the complete library; TypeRig's GUI scripts, panels and toolbars stay in kateliev/TypeRig .
title: typerig

text: python -m pip install typerig TypeRig needs Python 3.10 or newer and installs fonttools for font file I/O. The core needs no FontLab. Install it into FontLab's Python folder as well to use the FontLab proxies; see Install into FontLab .
title: Install

text: from typerig.core.objects.point import Point point = Point ( 10 , 20 ) + Point ( 2 , 3 ) print ( point . x , point . y ) # 12.0 23.0
title: Quick start

text: Inside FontLab, use the proxy layer on the current glyph: from typerig.proxy.fl.objects.glyph import eGlyph glyph = eGlyph () # wraps the current glyph print ( glyph . name , glyph . getBounds ())
title: Examples

text: Proxy modules need their host API (FontLab, or Glyphs for the Glyphs proxies). Licence: Mozilla Public License 2.0 (upstream TypeRig). Reference: typerig .

text: Glyport constructs a GlyphsApp module for each adapted Glyphs script. Its Glyphs object belongs to that script's FontLab context. Use the Glyphs scripting guide for the supported script entry point and the Glyport guide for installation and adaptation. The source-backed fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp reference documents make_glyphsapp_module , the factory that assembles this runtime namespace. The constructed GlyphsApp module and the importable helper namespace fontlab_glyport.glyphsapp have distinct roles: the former exposes the per-script compatibility API; the latter provides its factory and supporting functions. Runtime exports depend on the supplied script context and bridges. This page preserves the reference/GlyphsApp.html entry point. Source-derived factory documentation does not establish native FontLab workflow acceptance.
title: GlyphsApp

text: PythonQt is the Qt binding built into FontLab. Scripts use it to build dialogs, panels and other user interface, and to work with Qt values such as points, rectangles, colours and fonts that the FontLab API returns. PythonQt.QtCore , PythonQt.QtGui and the other modules below expose the Qt classes that FontLab's build provides; the classes in this module are PythonQt's own helpers.
title: Overview

text: Module Summary Config Build configuration flags of the PythonQt binding. Debug Debugging helpers of the PythonQt binding. Qt All Qt classes in one namespace, combining QtCore, QtGui and the other modules. QtCore Core non-GUI classes: strings, byte arrays, points, rectangles, timers, signals and slots, the event loop. QtGui Widgets, dialogs, layouts, painting (QPainter, QPainterPath), images, colours and fonts. QtNetwork TCP, UDP and HTTP networking classes. QtOpenGL OpenGL widget and context classes. QtSvg SVG rendering and generation (QSvgRenderer, QSvgGenerator, QSvgWidget). QtUiTools Loading Qt Designer .ui files at runtime (QUiLoader). QtXmlPatterns XQuery and XPath evaluation over XML. private Wrappers for FontLab's own Qt-based classes; which ones are registered depends on what the session has used.

text: The FontLab Python API is a C++/Python binding layer: The class articles document registered names, member kinds, calling conventions and property access. Some APIs depend on build flags. The separate fontgate module and inherited PythonQt/Qt APIs are outside this inventory. CurrentFont() returns fgFont , and CurrentGlyph() returns fgGlyph . Use fl.flPackage(fg_font) or fl.flGlyph(fg_glyph) when calling the model APIs described by the fl* guides. Constructing a wrapper from an existing model object does not imply an independent geometry copy; use the appropriate clone() operation when a separate object is needed.
title: Architecture

text: Throughout the documentation, types use these conventions: Type Meaning str Python string (C++ QString ) float Python float (C++ double ) int Python integer bool Python bool QPointF Qt 2D point; use PythonQt.QtCore.QPointF unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion QRectF Qt rectangle; use PythonQt.QtCore.QRectF unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion QTransform 3×3 matrix — passed as a QTransform -like object QColor Qt color; use PythonQt.QtGui.QColor unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion list(T) Python list of type T T/None Returns T or Python None
title: Type Conventions

text: Registered methods take positional arguments unless their class article explicitly lists keyword support. Optional values shown as name=default in signatures do not by themselves imply keyword support. flNode documents its keyword-capable methods. Value-wrapper constructors document their own field-keyword initialization. Inherited registrations are documented in the base class article; each class article names its binding base where applicable. C++ inheritance alone does not guarantee that a base member is exposed in Python. Binding annotations record declared signatures and can be incomplete; implementation notes in the class articles qualify known differences. High-level FontLab editing API. flGlyph contains drawing layers, flLayer contains shapes, and flContour contains nodes. CurrentFont() and CurrentGlyph() access the active editing context. Source: FontLab Proteus API documentation

text: FontLab MCP tools for embedded Python. fontpr exposes the tools of FontLab's MCP server as ordinary functions inside FontLab's own Python. A script can call the same focused, validated operations that an external MCP client uses, without a network connection or a token. Calling convention: Every tool function takes keyword arguments only. Positional arguments are ignored, so fontpr.list_glyphs(font_id=1) works and fontpr.list_glyphs(1) does not pass font_id . fontpr.call(name, **kwargs) calls a tool by its MCP name; name must be a string (otherwise TypeError ), for example fontpr.call("list_glyphs", font_id=1) . fontpr.available() returns True once the MCP tools are ready. Before then every call raises fontpr.Error("MCP tools are not available yet.") . fontpr.list_tools() returns a list of tool metadata dicts ( name , description , inputSchema and the other MCP fields) for the running build. Blocked tools are left out, and the list is empty when tools are unavailable. Treat it as authoritative: the functions documented here come from one build and one specification. run_python and get_python_output are blocked: calling them through fontpr raises fontpr.Error , because a script is already running Python. Results: A tool error ( isError ) raises fontpr.Error with the tool's message. Otherwise the first text result is parsed as JSON and returned as a dict or list ; text that is not JSON is returned as str . Inspect payload fields such as success , status , changed , applied and persisted . A returned value does not by itself mean that the font changed. Targeting: font : Use font_id from list_fonts.fonts[].id or new_font.font.id. IDs are in-memory session IDs, not persistent file identifiers. font_id takes precedence; invalid ID errors rather than falling back. font_name : First case-insensitive substring match against full, family or PostScript name. Ambiguous matches are not rejected; use IDs for writes. default_font : Active package when selectors are omitted. Selection is shared with the GUI and every client. glyph : Use exact glyph_name, not a character/code point; @ is glyph at. Some internal handlers fall back to current glyph, but advertised required glyph_name should always be supplied. actions : Prefer explicit nonempty glyph_names for glyph actions. Omitted glyph_names uses current GUI selection only if every glyph belongs to the requested font; empty or malformed arrays fail rather than falling back. layers : layer_name (get_glyph construction/build_glyph/anchors) is an exact layer name. layer_mode (run_actions) is active/visible/masters. master_name (font info/kerning) is a separate selector; never substitute these for one another. units : Geometry, widths, sidebearings, anchors and kerning are font units, not pixels. Angles are degrees. Use get_font_metrics for UPM and master names. examples : Numeric ID 101 and names H, A, V, Regular are illustrative. Replace with discovered IDs and names before executing examples. Working rules: Discover tools and open fonts first; collect an explicit target ID and relevant glyph/layer/master names. Use explain for UI, preference and action meaning; list_actions for actual action IDs. Prefer focused getters/setters and construction tools. Use run_actions for whole glyphs; run_python/fontpr for explicitly requested Python or edits not expressible by focused tools. Use basic glyph summaries first. Page results and filter exactly; do not request full VFJ merely to count contours. Read before replacing; get_glyph full VFJ must be preserved except intended edits when passed to set_glyph. Use build_glyph dry_run when a staged preview is needed to assess the result. Only set replace:true after inspecting the target. Re-read affected state after every mutation. Do not reuse cached read evidence after writes. Use explicit output paths and default overwrite:false for batch copies. Verify the destination, then close only fonts owned by the batch. No global transaction or universal MCP undo tool exists. Keep backups for destructive workflows. Preserve failed fonts for inspection. Never invent tool names such as save_font_as, new_glyph, export_font, select_master, undo or redo. They are not currently advertised. Distinguish MCP behavior from built-in Chat policy: Chat enables Python with /python on or an explicit request such as allow Python; authorization lasts until /python off or clearing the chat. It keeps native tools available and adds confirmation/budgeting; external MCP does not add those prompts. Known limitations: non-atomic: run_actions and arbitrary Python can change state before an error. The contour-loss check in run_actions detects loss after execution and does not undo it. Inputs for a kerning-class membership patch are validated before changing side flags, but there is no general transaction guarantee. save-copy: Explicit saves preserve source location and dirty state. After saving a new font to a copy path, save_font without path and close_font(save=true) still have no original save location. After verifying the copy, close_font(save=false). Existing VFJP directories cannot be overwritten. blocking: Python tracing (5 seconds by default, configurable with set_mcp_settings) is cooperative and cannot interrupt a blocked C++/extension call. A bridge timeout does not prove an operation stopped. Source: FontLab MCP specification

they must be obtained from the FontLab's window classes Canvas() - generic constructor, creates an empty Canvas Canvas(Canvas) - copy constructor ATTRIBUTES: delta (Point) - horizontal shift during coordinates transformation scale (Point(float)) - scaling during coordinates transformation width (integer, read-only) - width of the canvas in pixels height (integer, read-only) - height of the canvas in pixels draw_style (integer, write-only) - sets current drawing mode (copy, XOR, invert etc.) pen_color (integer, write-only) - sets current pen color pen_style (integer, write-only) - sets current pen style (solid, dashed etc.) brush_color (integer, write-only) - sets current brush color brush_style (integer, write-only) - sets current brush style (solid, patterned etc.) text_color (integer, write-only) - sets color for a text bk_color (integer, write-only) - sets color for a text background bk_mode (integer, write-only) - sets background mode for a text output (transparent or opaque) OPERATIONS: METHODS MoveTo(Point p) | (x, y) - moves current position to p or (x, y) coordinates LineTo(Point p) | (x, y) - draws a straight line to the position p or (x, y) CurveTo(Point p0, Point p1, Point p2) - draws a 3th-order Bezier curve from the current point to points p0, p1, p2 SplineTo(Point p0, Point p1) - draws a 2th-order Bezier curve from the current point to points p0, p1 Ellipse(Rect r) | (Point p0, Point p1) | (x0, y0, x1, y1) - draws a filled ellipse defined by the Rect r, points p0 and p1 or set of coordinates Rectangle(Rect r) | (Point p0, Point p1) | (x0, y0, x1, y1) - draws a filled rectangle defined by the Rect r, points p0 and p1 or set of coordinates Convert(Point p) - converts coordinates from the source coordinate space to screen coordinates UnConvert(Point p) - converts screen coordinates to the currently defined coordinate space FitGlyph(Rect r, Glyph g) | (Rect r, Glyph g, WeightVector w) - recalculates parameters of coordinate conversion function to fit glyph g into rectangle r using currently selected options. FillGlyph(Glyph g) | (Glyph g, WeightVector w) - fills the glyph g using current coordinate transformation. OutlineGlyph(Glyph g) | (Glyph g, WeightVector w) - draws the glyph g outline using current coordinate transformation.
